title: 1 HENRY IV
author: Shakespeare
summary: A history play of rebellion against Henry IV, balancing the court and battlefield against the Eastcheap tavern world of Falstaff; it traces Prince Hal's education toward kingship, climaxing at Shrewsbury with the defeat of Hotspur.

title: 2 HENRY IV
author: Shakespeare
summary: A history play of the dying Henry IV and the final maturation of Prince Hal, ending with his accession as Henry V and the cold rejection of Falstaff; pervaded by themes of sickness, mortality, time, and the burden of rule.

title: A Boston Ballad (1854)
author: Whitman
summary: A bitter satire on the Fugitive Slave rendition in Boston, summoning Revolutionary ghosts and mockingly crowning King George's skeleton; free-verse on liberty betrayed, ghosts and political critique.

title: A Broadway Pageant
author: Whitman
summary: The Japanese envoys' procession down Broadway becomes a vision of the ancient Orient meeting young America; free-verse on the city, history, and global democratic union.

title: A Carol Closing Sixty-Nine
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse song of the aged, paralyzed poet still affirming God, freedom, country and faith; themes of old age, mortality, patriotism and faith.

title: A Christmas Greeting
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A fraternal greeting to a Brazilian brother nation, affirming the democratic aim and the light of nationhood as more shining than Cross or Crown.

title: A Clear Midnight
author: Whitman
summary: A four-line free-verse lyric of the soul's nocturnal flight toward night, sleep, death and the stars; themes of the soul, night and death.

title: A Descent Into the Maelstrom
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: A frame-narrative sea tale in which an old fisherman recounts surviving the Norwegian whirlpool by rational observation; explores terror, the sublime, and reason against the destructive power of nature.

title: A Dream
author: Poe
summary: A short early lyric contrasting a cherished 'holy dream' of vanished joy with waking grief; meditates on memory, melancholy, and the light of Truth amid darkness.

title: A Farm Picture
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order

title: A Florentine Tragedy
author: Wilde
summary: Renaissance-Florence blank-verse fragment in which the merchant Simone discovers his wife Bianca with the prince Guido and kills the lover in a duel, ending in jealous, blood-bought desire.

title: A Font of Type
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse metapoetic lyric on the latent power of typeface, the unspoken words slumbering as ocean waves; themes of writing, the book and creative potency.

title: A Glimpse
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Bar-room vignette of two men content to sit hand in hand amid noise; comradeship, the city, the common man and silent intimacy.

title: A Hand-Mirror
author: Whitman
summary: A stark free-verse confrontation with one's own corrupted body and soul reflected in a mirror; the mirror motif, decay, mortality and self-examination.

title: A Leaf for Hand in Hand
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Offering of a 'leaf' to all natural persons, wishing comrades commonly walk hand in hand; comradeship, leaves, hands, the common man and democracy.

title: A Lover’s Complaint
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A rhyme-royal narrative complaint in which a forsaken maid, overheard by an aged shepherd, laments her seduction and ruin by a beautiful, deceitful young man; a lyric of unrequited love, deception and faded beauty.

title: A MIDSUMMER NIGHT’S DREAM
author: Shakespeare
summary: A festive romantic comedy in which four Athenian lovers, a fairy king and queen, and a troupe of rude mechanicals are entangled by love-magic in an enchanted wood; it celebrates imagination, dream, and the irrationality of desire while mocking theatrical illusion.

title: A March in the Ranks Hard-Prest, and the Road Unknown
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A night-march halts at a church turned field-hospital, a scene of blood, surgery and a dying lad; the horror and cost of war witnessed firsthand.

title: A Noiseless Patient Spider
author: Whitman
summary: Famous two-stanza lyric comparing a spider casting filaments into the void to the soul ceaselessly flinging gossamer threads to connect with the spheres.

title: A Paumanok Picture
author: Whitman
summary: Imagist seascape of Long Island fishermen drawing a seine of mossbonkers onto the beach; a still, concrete picture of sea and labor.

title: A Persian Lesson
author: Whitman
summary: A Sufi greybeard in a Persian rose-garden teaches that Allah is immanent in every atom and that the central urge of all things is to return to their divine source.

title: A Prairie Sunset
author: Whitman
summary: An imagistic prairie sunset of pure luminous color fighting the silent shadows to the last.

title: A Predicament
author: Poe
summary: A grotesque satire (companion to 'How to Write a Blackwood Article') in which Signora Psyche Zenobia is decapitated by a giant clock-hand; parodies sensational magazine fiction through black comedy and the grotesque.

title: A Promise to California
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Promise to travel west to teach 'robust American love'; comradeship bound to westward expansion, the road, and democratic nationhood.

title: A Riddle Song
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse riddle poem on an ineffable two-word secret pursued by all humanity; themes of inexpressibility, the quest, love and the soul.

title: A Sight in Camp in the Daybreak Gray and Dim
author: Whitman
summary: At dawn the speaker uncovers three dead on stretchers, the last seeming the face of Christ himself; war-death sanctified, the dead soldier as Christ-figure.

title: A Song for Occupations
author: Whitman
summary: Addressed to workmen and workwomen, asserting the divinity of the common laborer and the soul over institutions; a free-verse catalogue of trades and tools affirming democratic equality.

title: A Song of Joys
author: Whitman
summary: An ecstatic free-verse catalogue of the joys of work, the body, the sea, and the senses, culminating in the joy of death and the soul's transcendence of the material.

title: A Song of the Rolling Earth
author: Whitman
summary: Words are the substantial things of earth and body, not printed signs; a free-verse meditation on nature, the soul, the inexpressible, and the self's own immortality.

title: A Tale of Jerusalem
author: Poe
summary: A short satirical biblical burlesque in which Jewish priests besieged by Pompey's Romans haul up an unclean hog instead of a sacrificial lamb; a comic clash of religion and mockery during the Roman siege of Jerusalem.

title: A Twilight Song
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: By twilight firelight the poet musters the mystic roll of countless unknown Civil War dead, dedicating a special verse to embalm their unwritten names in love.

title: A Valentine
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: An acrostic love poem concealing a lady's name in its lines; a playful puzzle-poem on love, riddle, and the link between names, truth, and poetry.

title: A Voice from Death
author: Whitman
summary: A meditation on a catastrophic flood (Johnstown) as a voice from Death, ministering destruction yet eliciting human sympathy and recalling nature's resistless elemental power.

title: A Woman Waits for Me
author: Whitman
summary: Frank celebration of sex containing all and of procreation begetting strong future Americans; lust, the body, marriage/procreation, America.

title: A Woman of No Importance
author: Wilde
summary: Wilde's 1893 society comedy turning on the dandy Lord Illingworth, his abandoned former lover Mrs. Arbuthnot and their illegitimate son; an epigram-laden satire of the English aristocracy that exposes the double standard punishing the fallen woman while the man goes free.

title: ALL IS TRUE - (HENRY VIII)
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late history play (with Fletcher) dramatizing the fall of Buckingham, Wolsey's rise and disgrace, Katherine's repudiation and Anne Boleyn's rise toward Elizabeth's birth; themes are the falls of the great, power and ambition, conscience, and providential history.

title: ALL’S WELL THAT ENDS WELL
author: Shakespeare
summary: A Jacobean 'problem play' comedy in which Helen, a physician's daughter, wins the reluctant aristocrat Bertram through a cure, an enforced marriage and the bed-trick; central themes are unrequited love, class disparity, virtue versus rank, and an uneasily happy resolution.

title: ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA
author: Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's Roman tragedy in blank verse dramatizing the ruinous passion of Mark Antony and the Egyptian queen Cleopatra, set against the disintegrating triumvirate; its themes are love as empire-destroying desire, the conflict of Rome and Egypt, and transcendent death.

title: AS YOU LIKE IT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A pastoral romantic comedy in which exiles flee a usurping court to the Forest of Arden, where Rosalind, disguised as a youth, tutors Orlando in love; it celebrates the green world, disguise, and the contrast of court and country, voicing the Seven Ages of Man.

title: Aboard at a Ship’s Helm
author: Whitman
summary: A warning bell saves a ship from wreck, opening into the ship of body and soul voyaging on; free-verse lyric on the sea, ships, the journey and the soul.

title: Adieu to a Soldier
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Farewell to a comrade-soldier whose mission is fulfilled while the poet marches on to fiercer spiritual battles; comradeship, war, and the road of struggle.

title: After the Dazzle of Day
author: Whitman
summary: Short lyric: only after day's dazzle and clangor fade do stars and the true inner symphony emerge.

title: After the Sea-Ship
author: Whitman
summary: The wake of a sea-ship and its frolicking procession of waves; a sensuous free-verse lyric on the sea, ships, water and motion.

title: After the Supper and Talk
author: Whitman
summary: A meditation on death as the lingering, reluctant final farewell of a friend departing into darkness on a journey of no return.

title: Ages and Ages Returning at Intervals
author: Whitman
summary: The phallic, immortal chanter of Adamic songs returning through ages, bathing his songs in sex; eternal return, the body, lust, immortality.

title: Ah Poverties, Wincings, and Sulky Retreats
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric figuring life as a war against inner foes that the true self will overcome; themes of the self and soul, struggle and ultimate victory.

title: Al Aaraaf
author: Poe
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: A long, allusive cosmic poem set on Tycho Brahe's wandering star, an afterworld of pure Beauty where the angel Nesace and lovers Angelo and Ianthe dwell; explores beauty, knowledge, death, and the gulf between earthly and ideal.

title: All Is Truth
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: A meditative free-verse lyric affirming that all things, even apparent lies, partake of universal truth; themes of truth, identity and the self and cosmos.

title: Alone
author: Poe
summary: An early confessional lyric on the poet's lifelong sense of difference and isolation from childhood; themes of alienation, melancholy, and a visionary apartness drawn from nature's storms.

title: America
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Personifies America as an enduring towering Mother of equality, freedom and law, a patriotic celebration.

title: Among the Multitude
author: Whitman
summary: Within the crowd one 'lover and perfect equal' picks out the poet by secret signs; love, identity, the city and mutual recognition.

title: An Army Corps on the March
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A compact battlefield image of dust-covered ranks and rumbling artillery pressing on under the sun; the relentless mass-motion of an army.

title: An Enigma
author: Poe
summary: A sonnet that both mocks shallow sonnets and conceals a lady's name acrostically; reflects on transience, immortality through naming, and the craft of the poetic riddle.

title: An Ideal Husband
author: Wilde
summary: Wilde's society comedy of political corruption and blackmail, contrasting public and private morality, with the dandy Lord Goring as raisonneur and a buried secret threatening a statesman's career.

title: An Old Man’s Thought of School
author: Whitman
summary: Occasional poem for a school inauguration; sees children as immortal ships launching on the soul's voyage and links education to America's future.

title: Annabel Lee
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A musical ballad lamenting the death of a beautiful young beloved in a kingdom by the sea, whose love outlasts death; centers on love, grief, the death of a beautiful woman, and undying devotion.

title: Are You the New Person Drawn Toward Me?
author: Whitman
summary: Interrogative warning to a would-be lover that the poet is not the ideal imagined; identity, illusion (maya), and the uncertainty of love and friendship.

title: As Adam Early in the Morning
author: Whitman
summary: Closing Children of Adam lyric: the speaker as Adam at dawn inviting touch of his unashamed body; the body, innocence, dawn, Eden.

title: As Consequent, Etc.
author: Whitman
summary: Prefatory poem of Autumn Rivulets figuring the poet's songs as autumn streams flowing to the mystic ocean of time and death; rivers, sea, shells, and continuity of life.

title: As I Ebb’d with the Ocean of Life
author: Whitman
summary: Walking the shore in autumn the poet despairs, feeling himself mere drift and debris, calling the sea his father; free-verse crisis-lyric on doubt, the self, mortality and nature.

title: As I Lay with My Head in Your Lap Camerado
author: Whitman
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A confessional address to a comrade: the poet's restless dangerous words unsettle settled laws, urging onward without knowing the destination; comradeship, rebellion and uncertain quest.

title: As I Ponder’d in Silence
author: Whitman
summary: A phantom of old poets demands the theme of war; Whitman answers that his book too sings a greater war for body and soul. Free-verse poetic-vocation lyric.

title: As I Sit Writing Here
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse lyric fearing that the aches and ennui of old age filter into his songs; themes of old age, writing and melancholy.

title: As I Walk These Broad Majestic Days
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse lyric set in postwar days of peace asserting the poet's spiritual realities above science and industry; themes of democracy, war's aftermath and the soul.

title: As I Watch the Ploughman Ploughing
author: Whitman
summary: Quatrain reading agricultural labor as an analogy for mortality: life is the tillage and death the harvest according.

title: As If a Phantom Caress’d Me
author: Whitman
summary: Brief shore lyric in which a loved phantom that caressed the speaker vanishes in glimmering light, leaving only hateful mocking presences.

title: As They Draw to a Close
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse valedictory summing the aims of his songs and accepting death as the equal of life; themes of the soul, death and the book.

title: As Toilsome I Wander’d Virginia’s Woods
author: Whitman
summary: In autumn woods the speaker finds an unknown soldier's grave with a scrawled epitaph that haunts him for years; an elegy of remembrance and comradeship.

title: As at Thy Portals Also Death
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A free-verse elegy and verbal tombstone to the poet's dead mother as the ideal woman; themes of death, grief, motherhood and memory.

title: As the Greek’s Signal Flame
author: Whitman
summary: Like an ancient Greek beacon hailing a hero, the poet lifts a kindled brand from Manhattan's shore to an Old Poet.

title: As the Time Draws Nigh
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric anticipating the poet's death and the silencing of his song; themes of mortality, the book and the soul.

title: Ashes of Soldiers
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A free-verse elegy summoning the phantom dead of both armies and vowing undying love to fertilize the earth; themes of war's cost, death, comradeship and immortality.

title: Assurances
author: Whitman
summary: Litany of 'I do not doubt' affirmations of cosmic order, the limitless soul, and that Heavenly Death provides for all; serene faith against doubt.

title: Beat! Beat! Drums!
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A pounding incantatory war-song in which drums and bugles shatter church, school, marriage and ordinary life; war's intrusion on the peaceful world.

title: Beginners
author: Whitman
summary: Meditation on great original souls who appear at intervals, dear and dreadful, fated and misvalued; the prophet/outcast and the price of greatness.

title: Beginning My Studies
author: Whitman
summary: Ecstatic wonder at the first step of consciousness, sense and motion; joy, wonder and gratitude, the sublime in the ordinary. Short free-verse lyric.

title: Behold This Swarthy Face
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Self-portrait of the unadorned poet kissed by a Manhattanese comrade; the 'salute of American comrades land and sea'; comradeship, the body, the common man.

title: Berenice
author: Poe
summary: A gothic horror tale in which the monomaniac Egaeus, obsessed with his dying cousin Berenice's teeth, violates her premature grave to extract them; explores madness, obsession, decay, and the horror of the body.

title: Bivouac on a Mountain Side
author: Whitman
summary: An imagistic night-camp scene: a halting army, scattered camp-fires, shadowy men and horses, and over all the eternal stars; war set against cosmic permanence.

title: Bon-Bon
author: Poe
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A comic tale in which a vain restaurateur-philosopher is visited by the Devil, who eats souls and declines to buy Bon-Bon's; a satire on metaphysics, wine, and the philosopher's pride through a Faustian comedy.

title: Bravo, Paris Exposition!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: An occasional greeting wafting America's love and good-will across the sea to the Paris Exposition, celebrating fraternity among nations and inherited debts to forebears.

title: Broadway
author: Whitman
summary: The crowded New York street as a teeming theatre of human passions, an unspeakable show and lesson of life.

title: By Blue Ontario’s Shore
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: Long programmatic ode in which a phantom commands the poet to chant the throes of Democracy; a manifesto of the American bard, the self, the nation, and the cost of the secession war.

title: By Broad Potomac’s Shore
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric invoking Virginia's spring, blood-red roses and deathless grass to perfume the poet's book; themes of nature, spring and the immortality of verse.

title: By the Bivouac’s Fitful Flame
author: Whitman
summary: By a flickering camp-fire the speaker's thoughts wind in solemn procession over life and death, home and the absent loved; a meditative night-camp lyric.

title: CARDENIO - A BRIEF ACCOUNT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: An editorial prose account of the lost play Cardenio, attributed to Shakespeare and Fletcher and based on a Don Quixote episode; it summarizes a tragicomedy of rape, betrayed friendship, a disguised wronged heroine, madness for revenge, repentance and reconciliation.

title: CORIOLANUS
author: Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's last Roman tragedy in austere blank verse, on the proud warrior Caius Marcius Coriolanus whose contempt for the plebeians brings banishment and his vengeful alliance with Rome's enemies; themes are pride, class conflict, honour, and the politics of the state.

title: CYMBELINE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late tragicomic romance set in legendary Roman-era Britain, weaving a wager on Innogen's chastity, banishment, disguise, a wicked queen, and the descent of Jupiter into a web of miraculous reunions and reconciliations; themes are fidelity, jealousy, providence and restoration.

title: Camps of Green
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A free-verse lyric extending the soldiers' bivouac into the universal camp of the dead beneath the grass; themes of death, war, sleep and comradeship.

title: Cavalry Crossing a Ford
author: Whitman
summary: An imagistic miniature of a cavalry line snaking across a silvery river, arms flashing and guidon flags fluttering; a painterly battlefield scene.

title: Chanting the Square Deific
author: Whitman
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: Four-sided godhead chant voicing in turn the stern Father (Jehovah/Brahm/Saturn), the Christ-consolator, defiant Satan, and the all-pervading Santa Spirita soul.

title: City of Orgies
author: Whitman
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Manhattan poem declaring it is not the city's spectacles but the flashing eyes of lovers offering love that repay the poet; the city, eyes, love and desire.

title: City of Ships
author: Whitman
summary: An apostrophe to warlike Manhattan, city of ships and tides, whose song is now red war; an urban patriotic war-chant.

title: Come Up from the Fields Father
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: An elegiac narrative: a letter from the front announces the only son's death amid an autumnal Ohio farm; the grief of the bereaved mother. War's cost on the home front.

title: Complete Prose Works: Specimen Days and Collect, November Boughs and Goodbye My Fancy
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Whitman's collected prose: autobiographical Specimen Days, Civil War hospital memoranda, nature notes, and literary essays celebrating democracy, the common people, and nature.

title: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand

title: Continuities
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Nothing is ever truly lost; body, sun and frozen clods all return with spring, an affirmation of immortality and eternal renewal.

title: Crossing Brooklyn Ferry
author: Whitman
summary: Meditation across time uniting the poet with future ferry-crossers; the city, the river/sea, the crowd, time and the bond between self and future others.

title: Darest Thou Now O Soul
author: Whitman
summary: Lyric address summoning the soul to walk into the unknown region beyond death, where only Time and Space remain and the self bursts forth fulfilled.

title: De Profundis
author: Wilde
summary: Long prison letter charting Wilde's spiritual development through sorrow, humility and conversion, with Christ reimagined as the supreme individualist and romantic artist.

title: Death of General Grant
author: Whitman
summary: Elegy for General Grant, a hero withdrawing from history's stage of war and peace alongside Lincoln and Lee.

title: Delicate Cluster
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Drum-Taps apostrophe to the American flag as 'flag of life' and 'flag of death,' fusing battle, patriotism, and a maternal sacred emblem.

title: Diddling
author: Poe
summary: A mock-scientific satirical essay defining man as 'an animal that diddles' and cataloguing petty swindles; a comic anatomy of deception, the trickster, and social satire.

title: Dirge for Two Veterans
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A formal dirge for a father and son fallen together, buried in a double grave under a phantom moon to the music of drums and bugles; grief, mourning and the dead-march.

title: Dream-Land
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: A visionary lyric describing a journey to a weird, melancholy realm ruled by an Eidolon named Night, out of Space and Time; explores dream, death, memory, and a haunted otherworld of grief.

title: Dreams
author: Poe
summary: Youthful lyric exalting dream-life over waking reality, mingling melancholy, imagination, and a longing for an eternal visionary state.

title: Drum-Taps
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Whitman's Civil War poem cluster of free-verse lyrics: drums and marches, soldiers and comrades, the wound-dresser and hospital vigils, grief for the dead, and reconciliation. Sampling confirms central concerns with the cost of war, patriotism, loss, heroism, blood and death on the battlefield.

title: EDWARD III
author: Shakespeare
summary: Collaborative history play on Edward III's wars against Scotland and France (Crecy, Calais) and his attempted seduction of the virtuous Countess of Salisbury. Central themes: kingship, war and conquest, honour, chastity vs lust, mercy.

title: Earth, My Likeness
author: Whitman
summary: Poet sees in the impassive earth a hidden fierce force mirroring the inexpressible passion roused by an athlete-lover; nature, desire, the body and the inexpressible.

title: Eidolons
author: Whitman
summary: Metaphysical chant on eidolons (ideal images) as the permanent reality behind mutable matter; identity, immortality, mutability, the prophet-bard. Incantatory free verse.

title: Eighteen Sixty-One
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: An apostrophe to the war-year 1861 personified as an armed, sunburnt soldier striding across the continent; a patriotic war-poem of national crisis.

title: Eldorado
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: Ballad of a knight's lifelong quest for a golden land he never finds, ending with a pilgrim's counsel to ride down the Valley of the Shadow.

title: Election Day, November, 1884
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Names America's peaceful quadrennial election, not its landscapes, as its mightiest scene; democracy as a swordless conflict.

title: Eleonora
author: Poe
summary: Prose tale of innocent love in a paradisal valley, a dying beloved's vow, and a haunted narrator absolved for a second love.

title: Ethiopia Saluting the Colors
author: Whitman
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: An ancient enslaved woman, brought as a child across the sea, rises by the roadside to salute Sherman's colors marching to the sea; slavery, emancipation and the war.

title: Europe (The 72d and 73d Years of These States)
author: Whitman
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: On the 1848 revolutions: the people rise against kings and, though crushed, the martyrs' graves grow seed for freedom; free-verse on revolution, tyranny, martyrdom and liberty.

title: Evening Star
author: Poe
summary: Short lyric preferring the proud distant Evening Star to the cold moon, contrasting celestial lights with the speaker's heart.

title: Excelsior
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse boast in anaphoric questions asserting the speaker's surpassing happiness, boldness and love; themes of pride, joy and the self.

title: FANCIES AT NAVESINK
author: Whitman
summary: Eight-part sea sequence at Navesink meditating on tides, ebb and flow, death, rebirth, and the poet's life summed up against the ocean.

title: Faces
author: Whitman
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Catalogue of human faces good and grotesque, seeing through their cadaverous disguises to the deific soul behind each, ending in the justified mother of men.

title: Facing West from California’s Shores
author: Whitman
summary: The self as ancient child completing the circle of migration westward yet still seeking the unfound; the quest, the journey, identity, the sea.

title: Fairy-Land
author: Poe
summary: Fantastical lyric of waxing and waning moons descending over a dreamlike nocturnal landscape, blending imagination, night, and the supernatural.

title: Fast Anchor’d Eternal O Love!
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Ecstatic lyric that turns from 'O woman I love' to 'O man, O sharer of my roving life'; comradely love, desire, the sea and the open road.

title: First O Songs for a Prelude
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: The opening of Drum-Taps: Manhattan throws off peace and arms for the Civil War, drum-taps and bugles replacing opera; a patriotic mobilization song.

title: For Annie
author: Poe
summary: Lyric spoken from a deathlike repose, the fever of 'Living' conquered, soothed by the love of Annie and the peace of the grave.

title: For Him I Sing
author: Whitman
summary: Brief lyric raising the present on the past like a tree, fusing time and space and immortal laws; self-made man as law unto himself.

title: For You, O Democracy
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Programmatic Calamus lyric binding the American continent through the 'love of comrades'; fuses manly comradeship with democratic nationhood in free verse.

title: Four Beasts in One-The Homo-Cameleopard
author: Poe
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: Satirical sketch of the tyrant Antiochus Epiphanes parading as a beast in ancient Antioch, mocking flattery, tyranny, and mob folly.

title: France (the 18th Year of these States
author: Whitman
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A salute across the sea to revolutionary France, the bloody birth of liberty from tyranny; free-verse on revolution, patriotism and democratic hope.

title: From Far Dakota’s Canyons  (June 25, 1876)
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse elegiac sonnet-tribute to Custer's last stand at Little Bighorn, framed as heroic death; themes of war, heroism, the last stand and death.

title: From Montauk Point
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse seascape of restless waves forever seeking the shore from an eagle's vantage; themes of the sea, nature and ceaseless striving.

title: From Paumanok Starting I Fly Like a Bird
author: Whitman
summary: The poet soars bird-like over the whole continent to sing the idea of the inseparable Union and each of the States; a song of national unity.

title: From Pent-Up Aching Rivers
author: Whitman
summary: Long catalogue singing the phallus, procreation and the desire of body for body; lust, the body, love as inseparable union. Free verse.

title: Full of Life Now
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Closing Calamus poem addressing a reader centuries hence as comrade, the dead poet seeking the living; comradeship, immortality through verse, memory and time.

title: Germs
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: A compact free-verse epigram holding the germs of all forms, worlds and stars within a handful of space; nature, the cosmos, and latent universal life.

title: Give Me the Splendid Silent Sun
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A two-part lyric oscillating between a longing for rural solitude and Nature and a counter-craving for the turbulent crowds and drums of wartime Manhattan; Nature vs the city.

title: Gods
author: Whitman
summary: A litany naming the divine Comrade, the Ideal Man, Death, great ideas, Time, Space and stars as the poet's gods; free-verse hymn on the divine, death, comradeship and the soul.

title: Good-Bye My Fancy
author: Whitman
summary: A terse valedictory epigram in which the poet withholds his final word until its proper place arrives at the last.

title: Good-Bye My Fancy!
author: Whitman
summary: The poet's final tender farewell to his Fancy as the clock's ticking slows and the heart-thud stops, hoping the two blended selves go on together to true songs.

title: Grand Is the Seen
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Grand as the visible cosmos is, the unseen soul comprehending and lighting it is grander, more lasting and evolutionary than all the seen.

title: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume

title: HAMLET
author: Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's great revenge tragedy: the Danish prince, charged by his father's ghost to avenge a murder by his usurping uncle, confronts mortality, madness, deception and the gap between appearance and reality in soliloquy-driven blank verse.

title: HENRY V
author: Shakespeare
summary: A patriotic history play following the matured King Henry's invasion of France and victory at Agincourt; framed by a Chorus, it celebrates kingship, national unity, and heroic war while glancing at its human cost.

title: HENRY VI PART ONE
author: Shakespeare
summary: Early history play dramatizing England's losses in France after Henry V's death, the Joan la Pucelle episodes, and the seeds of the Wars of the Roses (the Temple Garden plucking of red and white roses). Central themes: civil discord, faction, kingship and the cost of war.

title: Halcyon Days
author: Whitman
summary: Old age's calm, ripe, blissful days valued above love, wealth or victory; serenity as life wanes.

title: Hast Never Come to Thee an Hour
author: Whitman
cluster: Vanitas · Contemptus Mundi · Vanity of Worldly Things
summary: A brief lyric questioning whether a sudden divine gleam has revealed the nothingness of worldly business, wealth and fashion; a vanitas-tinged meditation.

title: Here the Frailest Leaves of Me
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand

title: Hop-Frog
author: Poe
summary: Tale of an abused dwarf jester who exacts fiery revenge on a cruel king and his courtiers at a masquerade.

title: How Solemn As One by One (Washington City, 1865)
author: Whitman
summary: Watching returning ranks, the speaker sees behind each mask a kindred soul the bullet could never kill; the immortality of the soul and reverence for the common soldier.

title: How to Write a Blackwood Article
author: Poe
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Literary satire in which Signora Psyche Zenobia receives absurd instructions for manufacturing a sensational magazine 'intensity' article.

title: Hush’d Be the Camps To-Day (May 4, 1865
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Soldiers' mourning elegy for the dead commander Lincoln on his burial day, commissioning the poet to sing one verse for the heavy hearts of soldiers.

title: Hymn
author: Poe
summary: Devotional hymn to the Virgin Mary, invoking her grace through joy and the storms of fate at morn, noon, and twilight.

title: Hymn to Aristogeiton and Harmodius
author: Poe
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: Translation from the Greek celebrating the tyrant-slayers of Athens, glorifying liberty, heroism, and the deathless fame of avengers.

title: I Am He That Aches with Love
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand

title: I Dream’d in a Dream
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Vision of an invincible 'new city of Friends' ruled by robust love; comradeship as utopian civic ideal, dreams and the city.

title: I Hear America Singing
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Catalogue of working Americans each singing their own song; democracy, the common man, music and song, joyful labor. Free verse.

title: I Hear It Was Charged Against Me
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Poet disclaims destroying institutions, proposing instead 'the institution of the dear love of comrades' across the States; comradeship as civic foundation, democracy.

title: I Heard You Solemn-Sweet Pipes of the Organ
author: Whitman
summary: Sounds of organ, autumn winds and opera are surpassed by the pulse of the beloved heard against the body; love, music and song, autumn, the body.

title: I Saw Old General at Bay
author: Whitman
summary: A vignette of a hemmed-in general calling for volunteers who step forth cheerfully to risk their lives; heroism and self-sacrifice in war.

title: I Saw in Louisiana a Live-Oak Growing
author: Whitman
summary: Emblematic poem of a solitary live-oak that, unlike the poet, can utter joy without a friend near; nature, the tree as token of manly love, friendship and solitude.

title: I Sing the Body Electric
author: Whitman
summary: Extended hymn to the sacred male and female body, with the slave-auction section asserting the divinity of every body; the body, soul, democracy, social injustice. Free verse.

title: I Sit and Look Out
author: Whitman
summary: The poet looks out on all the sorrows, oppressions and shames of the world and is silent; free-verse catalogue of social injustice, grief and the witnessing self.

title: I Was Looking a Long While
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Finding the clue to history not in old fables but in Democracy and the average man of today; democracy, the common man, and the modern.

title: Imitation
author: Poe
summary: Early lyric figuring the speaker's life as a proud, dreamlike tide of vanished hope and visionary thought now passed away.

title: In Cabin’d Ships at Sea
author: Whitman
summary: Addresses his book as a ship voyaging the boundless sea; sea-voyage and open-road imagery, the book as faithful bark. Free verse.

title: In Paths Untrodden
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Opening Calamus poem resolving to sing only manly attachment and the need of comrades, away from the world's standards; comradeship, identity, nature.

title: In Youth I Have Known One
author: Poe
summary: Lyric on a youth in mystic communion with Nature drawn from sun and stars, with an appended Paean mourning a young dead beauty.

title: Interpolation Sounds
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Over a funeral service the poet hears interpolated the sudden sounds of Civil War battle, the clamor of arms and cavalry breaking into the solemn rite.

title: Israfel
author: Poe
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: Lyric praising the angel Israfel whose lyre outsings all creation, contrasting heavenly song with the mortal poet's earthbound music.

title: Italian Music in Dakota
author: Whitman
summary: A regimental band playing Italian opera in the wild Dakota night; nature listens, and art and wilderness find unexpected rapport.

title: JULIUS CAESAR
author: Shakespeare
summary: A Roman tragedy on the conspiracy and assassination of Caesar and its bloody aftermath, centred on Brutus's divided conscience; it dramatizes political idealism, rhetoric, fate and omens, and the cost of civil war.

title: Joy, Shipmate, Joy!
author: Whitman
summary: A short rhymed lyric celebrating death as a joyful ship setting sail from shore; themes of death as voyage, joy and the sea.

title: KING JOHN
author: Shakespeare
summary: A history play on the contested reign of King John, dramatizing dynastic legitimacy, political expediency (commodity), the murder of the boy Arthur, and conflict with Rome and France; the bastard Faustconbridge voices its cynical patriotism.

title: Kosmos
author: Whitman
summary: Definition of the cosmic person who contains all diversity, body and soul, all globes and eras; the self, the body, nature, and immortality.

title: L. of G.’s Purport
author: Whitman
summary: Whitman states the purport of Leaves of Grass as celebrating the immortal and the good, ending in sickness, poverty, and old age with Death dogging his steps.

title: LOVE’S LABOUR’S LOST
author: Shakespeare
summary: Witty courtly comedy in which the King of Navarre and his lords forswear women for study, then fall in love with the visiting Princess of France and her ladies; ends unconventionally with deferred marriage and the song of spring and winter. Central themes: love vs learning, wit and language, the play of appearance and vow-breaking.

title: LOVE’S LABOUR’S WON - A BRIEF ACCOUNT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Scholarly account of Shakespeare's lost comedy, attested by Francis Meres (1598) and a 1603 bookseller's fragment. As a comedy paired with Love's Labour's Lost it implies themes of romantic love and the fortunes of courtship; the account itself concerns textual transmission and the canon.

title: La Sainte Courtisane
author: Wilde
summary: Unfinished verse-drama in which the courtesan Myrrhina and the hermit Honorius exchange fates: she converts in the desert while he turns toward sin, dramatizing faith versus desire.

title: Lady Windermere's Fan
author: Wilde
summary: Wilde's 1892 society comedy in four acts satirising Victorian morality through the rigid 'good woman' Lady Windermere and the worldly Mrs. Erlynne (her secret mother), built on the fan, the dropped reputation, and an epigrammatic dialogue that dissolves the line between good and bad women.

title: Landor's Cottage
author: Poe
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Descriptive prose pendant to Arnheim, a wanderer's discovery of an exquisitely composed valley, cottage, and landscape-as-art.

title: Laws for Creations
author: Whitman
summary: Ars-poetica laws for American artists declaring man and woman as good as God; the artist and society, the self, and the divinity of the individual.

title: Leaves of Grass
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Whitman's master book: a sprawling free-verse epic of self and soul, body and democracy, America, nature, the sea, the open road, comradeship, sex, death and the cosmos. Includes Song of Myself and the Inscriptions; sampling confirms identity, the common man, joy, the sublime, immortality and the book-of-nature stance of the poet-prophet.

title: Lenore
author: Poe
summary: Elegiac dirge for the young dead Lenore, the bereaved lover rebuking false mourners and waiting her soul's flight to heaven.

title: Life
author: Whitman
summary: The undiscouraged struggling soul of man as an endless march, with an appended elegiac affirmation that all are 'going somewhere'.

title: Lingering Last Drops
author: Whitman
summary: A brief lyric on transience and origin: the late poems as the lingering concluding drops of a passing shower, drifting from an unknown source.

title: Lionizing
author: Poe
summary: Comic satire of the 'science of Noses' and literary celebrity, lampooning vanity, fashionable society, and pretentious erudition.

title: Lo, Victress on the Peaks
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Address to victorious Liberty after the war, offering not a proud poem but a cluster of night's darkness, blood-dripping wounds, and psalms of the dead.

title: Locations and Times
author: Whitman
summary: A short lyric on the self that corresponds to all places, times, forms and colors; a meditation on identity and the soul's affinity with the world.

title: Long, Long Hence
author: Whitman
summary: A prophecy of poetic immortality: only after ages of accumulation and myriad readers will the poet's songs reach their fruition.

title: Long, Too Long America
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A brief lyric arguing that America must now learn from crises of anguish, not prosperity, to reveal what its people really are; war as national test.

title: Look Down Fair Moon
author: Whitman
summary: A four-line invocation to the sacred moon to bathe the ghastly swollen faces of the battlefield dead; war-death and mournful benediction.

title: Lord Arthur Savile's Crime
author: Wilde
summary: A comic society tale in which a young aristocrat, told by a cheiromantist that he is fated to commit murder, treats the prophecy as a moral duty to be discharged before marriage; a satire of fashionable London that inverts fate, conscience and guilt into farce.

title: Loss of Breath
author: Poe
summary: Grotesque comic tale of a man who literally loses his breath, is mangled, hanged, entombed, and revived, parodying horror sensationalism.

title: MACBETH
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Guilt · Conscience · Fate and Free Will
summary: Shakespeare's tragedy of overreaching ambition: spurred by witches' prophecy and his wife, Macbeth murders the king to seize the crown and is consumed by guilt, tyranny and bloodshed; themes of ambition, fate, conscience and the supernatural.

title: MEASURE FOR MEASURE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A 'problem play' / tragicomedy set in Vienna where the deputy Angelo's hypocritical demand for Isabella's chastity in exchange for her brother's life probes justice and mercy, power and corruption, sin, chastity and forgiveness.

title: MUCH ADO ABOUT NOTHING
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A romantic comedy of two courtships: the witty 'merry war' between Beatrice and Benedick, and the slandered Hero, nearly destroyed by Don John's deception; it turns on noting/eavesdropping, false report, and the recovery of honour.

title: MY 71st Year
author: Whitman
summary: At twilight the aged poet, like an old broken soldier answering roll-call after the Civil War, reports still alive and saluting the Officer over all.

title: Maelzel's Chess-Player
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: Analytical essay using step-by-step ratiocination to prove Maelzel's chess automaton is operated by a concealed human, not pure machine.

title: Mannahatta (My city’s fit and noble name resumed)
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom

title: Mannahatta
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse hymn to New York City celebrating its harbor, crowds, commerce and democratic energy; themes of the city, democracy and America.

title: Me Imperturbe
author: Whitman
summary: Self-poised speaker standing at ease in Nature, self-balanced for contingencies like trees and animals; identity, nature, the sublime calm.

title: Mediums
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: A prophetic free-verse forecast of future American bards who will report nature and illustrate democracy; themes of the poet as prophet, democracy and America.

title: Mellonta Tauta
author: Poe
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Satirical epistolary science-fiction set in 2848, a balloon-borne letter mocking democracy, scientific method and human progress; a manuscript-in-a-bottle frame satirizing the future's contempt for the past.

title: Memories
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume

title: Mesmeric Revelation
author: Poe
summary: Pseudo-scientific dialogue in which a dying mesmerized man reveals a metaphysics of God as 'unparticled matter,' the soul's immortality, and death as metamorphosis; ends with the sleep-waker's death.

title: Metzengerstein
author: Poe
summary: Gothic horror tale of feuding Hungarian houses and metempsychosis: a demonic horse embodying a dead rival drives the dissolute young Baron to a fiery, fated doom.

title: Miracles
author: Whitman
summary: Catalog declaring every ordinary thing a miracle, from Manhattan streets to the sea and stars; wonder and gratitude, nature, and the divinity of the everyday.

title: Mirages
author: Whitman
summary: A visionary lyric of mirage-scenes seen at dawn or dusk, vivid spectral images of camps, homes, weddings, and funerals appearing at the sky-edge.

title: Ms. Found in a Bottle
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: A rationalist narrator's manuscript of a doomed sea voyage: storm, a spectral ghost-ship crewed by aged phantoms, and a final plunge into a southern polar whirlpool toward forbidden knowledge.

title: My Canary Bird
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse lyric weighing great books against the simple joy of a caged bird's song; themes of nature, the book and joy.

title: My Legacy
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric contrasting a rich man's bequests with the poet's legacy of war remembrances bound in songs; themes of mortality, memory and the book.

title: My Picture-Gallery
author: Whitman
summary: The skull/mind imagined as a tiny round gallery holding all the world's tableaus of life and death, with the self as cicerone guide.

title: Myself and Mine
author: Whitman
summary: A defiant free-verse assertion of self-reliance, independence from laws and schools, and the poet's refusal to be expounded; the self, agitation, and democratic individualism.

title: Mystification
author: Poe
summary: A comic tale of the trickster Baron Ritzner von Jung, master of mystification, who humiliates a pompous duellist with a nonsense treatise and a decanter hurled at a mirror; satire of the duello and honor.

title: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom

title: Native Moments
author: Whitman
summary: Speaker embraces libidinous joys and consorts with the lawless and shunned, vowing to be their poet; lust, the outcast, the common man, joy.

title: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order

title: Never Bet the Devil your Head
author: Poe
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A satirical moral tale mocking the demand that fiction carry a moral: the reprobate Toby Dammit literally loses his head to a diabolical old gentleman after wagering it once too often. Satire of transcendentalism.

title: Night on the Prairies
author: Whitman
summary: Standing under prairie stars, the speaker absorbs immortality and peace, measures himself by space and eternity, and awaits what death will exhibit.

title: No Labor-Saving Machine
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Poet's modest legacy is not invention or wealth but 'a few carols' left for comrades and lovers; comradeship, art and the poet's vocation.

title: Not Heat Flames Up and Consumes
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Anaphoric lyric likening the soul's restless burning for the beloved to fire, sea-waves and wind-borne seeds; desire, comradely love, nature and the sea.

title: Not Heaving from My Ribb’d Breast Only
author: Whitman
summary: Anaphoric Calamus lyric of bodily longing ('O adhesiveness! O pulse of my life!') locating comradely love not in the body alone but in song; desire, self and soul, the body.

title: Not Meagre, Latent Boughs Alone
author: Whitman
summary: His bare wintry songs may yet burst into future spring leaf and fruit, love and faith blooming like roses.

title: Not Youth Pertains to Me
author: Whitman
summary: A self-portrait lyric: not youth, beauty or learning, but the nursing of dying soldiers and the making of these songs belong to the speaker; the poet as wartime nurse.

title: Not the Pilot
author: Whitman
summary: The poet declares himself more charged than pilot or pathfinder with composing a battle-call march for the States, years and centuries hence; the poet-as-prophet of the nation.

title: Now Finale to the Shore
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse farewell bidding the old Sailor depart on an endless cruise beyond return; themes of death as voyage, the sea and the journey.

title: Now Precedent Songs, Farewell
author: Whitman
summary: The aged poet bids farewell to his earlier songs, naming them as a strange procession born of his life's hot pulsing blood.

title: O Captain! My Captain!
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Rhymed, ballad-like elegy for Lincoln as the fallen captain of the ship of state who dies in the harbor of victory; grief amid public exultation.

title: O Hymen! O Hymenee!
author: Whitman
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Brief apostrophe to the god of marriage, the swift fierce moment that would kill if prolonged; desire, marriage, transience, love as near-death.

title: O Living Always, Always Dying
author: Whitman
summary: Lyric on the self continually dying and being reborn, content to leave behind the corpses of former selves and stride ahead, always living.

title: O Magnet-South
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse catalogue poem of nostalgic longing for the American South, evoking its rivers, flora and fauna; central themes are place, nostalgia and nature.

title: O Marie Louise (shew)
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A short lyric love poem on inexpressibility: the poet, who once boasted the 'power of words,' is struck speechless before the beloved's name, standing entranced on the threshold of dreams.

title: O Me! O Life!
author: Whitman
summary: A despairing question about the worth of life among foolish crowds, answered that you may contribute a verse; free-verse lyric on melancholy, identity and meaning.

title: O Star of France (1870-71)
author: Whitman
summary: Apostrophe to France as a crucified star and storm-tossed ship, mourning its woes yet prophesying rebirth; figures liberty, martyrdom and resurrection.

title: O Tan-Faced Prairie-Boy
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: A tender camp lyric: a silent prairie-boy recruit who gives nothing but a look worth more than all the gifts of the world; comradeship and tenderness between soldiers.

title: O You Whom I Often and Silently Come
author: Whitman
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Confession of a 'subtle electric fire' of unspoken desire kindled near the beloved; desire, the body and silent comradely love.

title: OTHELLO
author: Shakespeare
summary: A domestic tragedy in which the Moorish general Othello is poisoned by Iago's deception into murderous jealousy of his innocent wife Desdemona; central themes of jealousy, deception, the outsider, and appearance versus reality.

title: Of Him I Love Day and Night
author: Whitman
summary: Dream of searching burial-places for a dead beloved and finding every place full of the dead; resolves to dispense with graves, content with death everywhere.

title: Of That Blithe Throat of Thine
author: Whitman
summary: The poet takes the arctic bird's gay song as a lesson, singing cheerfully even amid the winter of old age.

title: Of the Terrible Doubt of Appearances
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Philosophical Calamus poem where epistemological doubt (appearance vs reality, identity beyond the grave) is answered not by reason but by the touch of the beloved comrade.

title: Offerings
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand

title: Old Age’s Lambent Peaks
author: Whitman
summary: A late valedictory lyric celebrating the elevated, illuminating vista of old age at life's golden twilight, where calmer perspective reveals the best of experience.

title: Old Age’s Ship & Crafty Death’s
author: Whitman
summary: Old age and death imagined as rival vessels closing in, met with defiant joy of strife as the poet's ship crowds on full sail toward the open sea.

title: Old Chants
author: Whitman
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A roll-call of the world's ancient poets and epics from Egypt, the Bible, Greece, and medieval legend, acknowledging America's debt to old poems and traditions.

title: Old Ireland
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Allegory of Ireland as a grieving ancient mother over an empty grave, consoled that her dead son lives risen in a new country; grief, resurrection, exile, and rebirth in America.

title: Old Salt Kossabone
author: Whitman
summary: A narrative of an old sailor ancestor who dies at his window the moment he sees a ship win free to the open sea.

title: Old War-Dreams
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A free-verse lyric with refrain recounting recurring nightmares of the Civil War dead; themes of war's cost, dreams, memory and death.

title: On Journeys Through the States
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Poet as wandering teacher-lover traveling the States and the world like the returning seasons; the open road, America, eternal return.

title: On the Beach at Night
author: Whitman
summary: A father comforts his weeping child as burial-clouds devour the stars, promising something more immortal than the stars; free-verse lyric on night, stars, mortality and immortality.

title: On the Beach at Night Alone
author: Whitman
summary: Alone by the night sea the poet perceives a vast similitude interlocking all things, times and beings; free-verse meditative lyric on the sea, stars, cosmic unity and the soul.

title: On, on the Same, Ye Jocund Twain!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A self-summing chant of the poet's life and recitative carried into old age, fusing personal soul with the democratic destiny of America and humanity.

title: Once I Pass’d Through a Populous City
author: Whitman
summary: Of a whole city only a clinging lover is remembered; love, memory, the city, parting. Short free-verse lyric.

title: One Hour to Madness and Joy
author: Whitman
summary: Ecstatic outburst of erotic abandon and freedom, a return to Paradise in one hour of fullness; lust, joy, madness, paradise. Free verse.

title: One’s-Self I Sing
author: Whitman
summary: Programmatic opening lyric of Leaves of Grass balancing the single self against the democratic en-masse, celebrating body and soul, male and female equally; free-verse manifesto.

title: Orange Buds by Mail from Florida
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Orange buds mailed across America to the poet's snowy Northern room as proof of the nation's broad expanse.

title: Osceola
author: Whitman
summary: A narrative elegy of the Seminole chief Osceola's death, who dons his war-dress and paint and silently bids farewell to wife and children before dying.

title: Others May Praise What They Like
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Brief credo praising nothing in art until it has inhaled the atmosphere of the Missouri and western prairie; nationalism, nature, and the artist's American grounding.

title: Our Old Feuillage
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A sprawling free-verse catalogue of the American continent, its regions, peoples, animals and labors, celebrating the unity-in-diversity of the democratic nation and the poet's identification with all of it.

title: Out from Behind This Mask (To Confront a Portrait)
author: Whitman
summary: The face as a mask and microcosm condensing the whole universe; the self, identity, the mirror/mask, and the poet greeting the reader across time.

title: Out of May’s Shows Selected
author: Whitman
summary: A catalogue of springtime natural beauty: blossoming orchards, wheat fields, morning freshness, lilac.

title: Out of the Cradle Endlessly Rocking
author: Whitman
summary: The poet's origin-myth: a boy on the Paumanok shore hears a mockingbird mourn its lost mate and the sea whisper 'death'; free-verse elegiac lyric on love, loss, death and the birth of the bard.

title: Out of the Rolling Ocean the Crowd
author: Whitman
summary: A lover figured as a drop from the rolling ocean, met and returned, yet ultimately one with the whole; love, the sea, transience, cosmic unity.

title: Outlines for a Tomb (G. P., Buried 1870)
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Elegy for a philanthropist millionaire (George Peabody) whose gifts conjure visions of provided-for laboring life; death, the tomb, charity, reform, and the common man.

title: Over the Carnage Rose Prophetic a Voice
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: A prophetic voice over the carnage declares that comradely affection, not laws or arms, will solve freedom's problems and bind the Union; love, comradeship and democracy.

title: PERICLES
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late dramatic romance (with George Wilkins) tracing Pericles' wanderings, shipwrecks, the loss and miraculous reunion with his daughter Marina and wife; central to it are the quest/sea-journey, suffering and patience, and providential restoration of the family.

title: Passage to India
author: Whitman
summary: Visionary ode joining the Suez Canal and Pacific railroad to a mystic voyage of the soul back to Asia, primal myth and God; engineering becomes spiritual quest.

title: Patroling Barnegat
author: Whitman
summary: A storm-tossed nocturne of figures patrolling a wild beach watching for a wreck; tightly rhythmic free verse on the sea, storm, night and death.

title: Paumanok
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse apostrophe to Long Island as sea-beauty between ocean and sound; themes of place, the sea and nature.

title: Pen, Pencil and Poison
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Critical biography of Wainewright, the artist-forger-poisoner, exploring the relation of art and crime, the artist and society, and the amorality of beauty.

title: Pensive on Her Dead Gazing
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse elegy in which the Mother of All bids earth absorb her slain sons and return them in grass centuries hence; themes of war's cost, death, nature and immortality.

title: Philosophy of Furniture
author: Poe
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A satirical aesthetic essay on interior decoration, attacking American 'glare,' glitter and the confusion of cost with beauty, then sketching an ideal tasteful crimson-and-gold chamber.

title: Pioneers! O Pioneers!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A martial chant urging the Western pioneers onward, the open road of conquest and labor, comradeship and death on the march; refrain-driven free verse on American expansion.

title: Poets to Come
author: Whitman
summary: Summons future poets to justify him; the speaker hurries back into darkness, expecting the main things from posterity. Prophet-poet, immortality through verse.

title: Prayer of Columbus
author: Whitman
summary: Dramatic monologue of a battered, shipwrecked Columbus on a savage shore praying to God in faith, doubt and visionary surrender at the end of life.

title: Proud Music of the Storm
author: Whitman
summary: Dream-vision in which all the music of nations, religions and nature pours through the sleeper's soul, ending in a charge to write poems bridging Life to Death.

title: Queries to My Seventieth Year
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse address questioning the coming year as a dim spectre bringing life or death; themes of mortality, old age and time.

title: Quicksand Years
author: Whitman
summary: Short lyric in which amid the dissolving quicksand of politics and shows only the strong-possessed Self/soul remains the final sure substance.

title: RICHARD DUKE OF YORK - (3 HENRY VI)
author: Shakespeare
summary: History play of the full Wars of the Roses: the see-saw struggle between York and Lancaster, the murder of York, the savagery of Margaret, the brief reign of Edward IV, and the emergence of the scheming Richard of Gloucester. Themes of revenge, ambition, kingship, fate, and the horror of civil war.

title: RICHARD II
author: Shakespeare
summary: Lyrical history play, entirely in verse, on the deposition and murder of the introverted King Richard II by Bolingbroke. Central themes: kingship and legitimacy, the divine right and fall of a king, identity, time, and the deposition's political resonance.

title: RICHARD III
author: Shakespeare
summary: History/tragedy charting the deformed Machiavel Richard of Gloucester's murderous rise to the throne and his fall at Bosworth. Central themes: ambition, power and corruption, conscience and guilt, the providential end of the Wars of the Roses.

title: ROMEO AND JULIET
author: Shakespeare
summary: Lyric tragedy of the star-crossed young lovers of feuding Verona houses, ending in their double suicide and the families' reconciliation. Central themes: romantic love, fate, the feud, the conflict of love and death, youth.

title: Race of Veterans
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A brief acclamation of a hardened race of victors and veterans, owning no law but its own; war's forging of a new American people.

title: Reconciliation
author: Whitman
summary: The speaker bends to kiss the white face of his dead enemy, a man divine as himself, as Death and Night wash the world clean; reconciliation, forgiveness and the brotherhood of the dead.

title: Recorders Ages Hence
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Address to future biographers asking to be remembered as 'the tenderest lover' of friends; self-portrait of comradely love, longing and dread of indifference.

title: Red Jacket (From Aloft)
author: Whitman
summary: The ghost of the Native chief Red Jacket looks down on a monument ceremony like one of Ossian's ghosts.

title: Reversals
author: Whitman
summary: Brief world-upside-down fragment inverting front and back, bidding the despised offer new propositions; a topos of social reversal.

title: Rise O Days from Your Fathomless Deeps
author: Whitman
summary: The poet, schooled by storms and wilderness, exults as warlike Democracy rises out of the cities; an ecstatic, stormy hymn to the war and democratic energy.

title: Roaming in Thought (After reading Hegel)
author: Whitman
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A two-line free-verse epigram after Hegel: the little Good hastens to immortality while the vast Evil merges and dies; on good vs evil, immortality and the natural order.

title: Romance
author: Poe
summary: A short lyric contrasting the gentle paroquet 'Romance' of childhood with the tumultuous 'Condor years' of adulthood, lamenting lost leisure for poetry; on memory, time and the poet's vocation.

title: Roots and Leaves Themselves Alone
author: Whitman
summary: Calamus poem offering scents, leaves and 'love-buds' that flower only if the reader brings warmth; nature, leaves, flowers and love as organic exchange.

title: SIR THOMAS MORE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A collaborative history play (with a Shakespearian scene) dramatizing Thomas More's quelling of the Ill May Day anti-foreigner riots, his rise to Lord Chancellor and his martyrdom for refusing the King's demands; central themes of obedience, conscience and martyrdom.

title: Sail out for Good, Eidolon Yacht!
author: Whitman
summary: Death imagined as the soul's eidolon-yacht sailing out from solid earth onto infinite free waters, framed as entrance to the truest voyage rather than an ending.

title: Salome
author: Wilde
summary: Wilde's one-act biblical tragedy in lyrical prose, dominated by the moon, the femme fatale's lust for the prophet Iokanaan, the dance of the seven veils, and the severed head, fusing desire and death.

title: Salut au Monde!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Vast catalogue-poem saluting all peoples, lands, religions and labors of the globe; cosmic democracy, comradeship of humankind, the sea, nature and the common man.

title: Savantism
author: Whitman
summary: Sees all results of everyday life nestling and obligated, the poet bringing his songs along like a father to ancestors; nature, time, identity.

title: Scenes From "Politian"
author: Poe
summary: An unfinished blank-verse verse-drama set in Renaissance Rome: the melancholy Earl Politian loves the ruined, vengeance-bound Lalage, swears to slay her betrayer Castiglione, building toward tragedy.

title: Scented Herbage of My Breast
author: Whitman
summary: Calamus meditation where leaves of the breast become tomb-leaves; love and death are inseparable, death the real reality; comradeship, death, melancholy.

title: Shadow-A Parable
author: Poe
summary: A plague-haunted company in ancient Ptolemais confronts a shadow speaking with the voices of the dead; a meditation on death, pestilence and the inescapable presence of the departed.

title: Shakspere-Bacon’s Cipher
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: A mystical lyric finding in every old song, object, and life a hidden cipher of meaning infolded behind appearance, the book of nature read for secret import.

title: Shut Not Your Doors
author: Whitman
summary: Demands a place in proud libraries for his war-born book whose drift is everything; the book/writing, the artist and society, war.

title: Silence
author: Poe
summary: A sonnet on the two-fold silence of body and soul, personifying the corporate silence of the grave ('No More') and warning of its nameless, dreadful counterpart.

title: Silence-A Fable
author: Poe
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A Demon recounts how he cursed a desolate Libyan landscape first with tumult then with silence, driving a solitary Roman figure to flight; a parable of desolation, the supernatural and the terror of silence.

title: Small the Theme of My Chant
author: Whitman
summary: Declares his theme: the single self and the en-masse, the whole human form, sung for the New World, reaching out to the reader.

title: So Long!
author: Whitman
summary: The valedictory closing poem of Leaves of Grass, announcing future democratic persons and the poet's bodily merging with the reader at death; themes of democracy, immortality of art and mortality.

title: Some Words with a Mummy
author: Poe
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: A galvanized Egyptian mummy, Count Allamistakeo, debates modern Americans and deflates 19th-century faith in progress, democracy and science; a satire blending the grotesque with critique of progress.

title: Sometimes with One I Love
author: Whitman
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Brief lyric on the fear of unreturned love resolved by the insight that out of unrequited love come these songs; love, unrequited love and the making of art.

title: Song
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A lyric addressed to a bride on her wedding day, whose blush kindles a fiercer flame of unrequited love and jealous loss in the speaker.

title: Song at Sunset
author: Whitman
summary: An ecstatic free-verse hymn of gratitude praising existence, the body, nature and the splendor of death at life's sunset; themes of wonder, joy and mortality.

title: Song for All Seas, All Ships
author: Whitman
summary: A recitative for the sailors of all nations and a spiritual flag of man elate above death; free-verse on the sea, ships, heroism and comradeship across nations.

title: Song of Myself
author: Whitman
summary: Whitman's great 52-section epic of the self merging with all humanity and nature; identity, body and soul, democracy, death and rebirth, ecstatic catalogues. Foundational free-verse epic.

title: Song of Prudence
author: Whitman
summary: Doctrine that every deed has consequences beyond death, charity and personal force the only investments; soul, immortality, conscience, and the body-soul bond.

title: Song of the Answerer
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: Portrait of the poet-prophet as universal 'Answerer' welcomed by all nations and trades, who settles justice and immortality; the poet as prophet, the common man, democracy and the artist.

title: Song of the Banner at Daybreak
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: A polyphonic dramatic lyric (Poet, Pennant, Child, Father, Banner) in which the war-flag, valueless yet supreme, demands devotion above peace and wealth; patriotism, war and sacrifice.

title: Song of the Broad-Axe
author: Whitman
summary: The axe as emblem of labor and civilization across history, from the European headsman to the American builder; a free-verse meditation on work, democracy, and the strong common person.

title: Song of the Exposition
author: Whitman
summary: Summoning the Muse from old Europe to modern industrial America, exalting labor, invention, the Union and peace over war; a patriotic free-verse ode to a new democratic culture.

title: Song of the Open Road
author: Whitman
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: Expansive free-verse hymn to the open road as image of freedom, self-reliance and democratic fellowship; the road, the journey, comradeship and the self.

title: Song of the Redwood-Tree
author: Whitman
summary: A dying California redwood chants its death-song, gladly yielding to a coming superber human race; free-verse on nature, mortality, the West, and democratic destiny.

title: Song of the Universal
author: Whitman
summary: A song of the universal good and the seed of perfection in all things, evolution toward the ideal and immortality, with America as the scheme's culmination; free-verse spiritual ode.

title: Sonnet 1
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Shakespearean sonnet opening the procreation sequence; urges the fair youth to breed so beauty's rose does not die, contrasting increase with self-consuming waste.

title: Sonnet 10
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Accuses the youth of murderous self-hate and pleads he make another self for love; beauty should live in offspring.

title: Sonnet 100
author: Shakespeare
summary: The poet rouses his forgetful muse to sing the beloved and satirize decay, giving fame faster than time's scythe wastes life.

title: Sonnet 101
author: Shakespeare
summary: The truant muse is taught to immortalize truth and beauty in verse, making the beloved outlive a gilded tomb.

title: Sonnet 102
author: Shakespeare
summary: Love strengthened though less shown; like Philomel the speaker holds his tongue lest common song dull its dear delight.

title: Sonnet 103
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The muse's poverty: the beloved's own mirror shows more than verse can; inexpressibility of beauty surpassing the poet's art.

title: Sonnet 104
author: Shakespeare
summary: Three years of seasons pass yet the friend seems unaged; beauty steals away imperceptibly like a dial-hand, hinting at mutability.

title: Sonnet 105
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Love defended against idolatry; the verse confined to constancy sings 'fair, kind, and true', love as quasi-religious devotion.

title: Sonnet 106
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Old chronicles of fair knights and ladies were but prophecies of the beloved; present eyes wonder but lack tongues to praise.

title: Sonnet 107
author: Shakespeare
summary: The mortal moon's eclipse endured; love survives and lives in verse as a monument outlasting tyrants' tombs of brass.

title: Sonnet 108
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Nothing new to write, yet like daily prayers the speaker repeats his love, eternal love that weighs not the dust of age.

title: Sonnet 109
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Denying falsehood despite absence and ranging; like a traveller he returns, calling the beloved his rose and his all.

title: Sonnet 11
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Nature's seal-and-print metaphor; wisdom and increase against age and cold decay, urging the youth to print more copies of himself.

title: Sonnet 110
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Confession of having played the motley and strayed; the wanderings proved the beloved his best of love, to whom he now returns confined.

title: Sonnet 111
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Blaming Fortune for public means that stained his name like the dyer's hand; he drinks bitter potions of penance, cured by the friend's pity.

title: Sonnet 112
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The friend's love fills the brand of vulgar scandal; the speaker, deaf as an adder to others, counts the world besides as dead.

title: Sonnet 113
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: In absence the eye is in the mind; every sight, crow or dove, mountain or sea, is shaped to the beloved's feature, the true mind making the eye untrue.

title: Sonnet 114
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: The mind crowned with the beloved drinks flattery as alchemy, turning monsters to cherubins; appearance and love's deceiving eye.

title: Sonnet 115
author: Shakespeare
summary: Earlier verses lied saying he could not love more; reckoning time's tyranny, love is a babe that still doth grow.

title: Sonnet 116
author: Shakespeare
