cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The marriage of true minds: love as an ever-fixed mark and guiding star, unshaken by tempests and not time's fool even to the edge of doom.

title: Sonnet 117
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The speaker confesses neglect and wandering ('hoisted sail to all the winds') but pleads he strove only to prove the constancy of the beloved's love.

title: Sonnet 118
author: Shakespeare
summary: Medicinal conceit: seeking bitter sauces to whet appetite, the speaker sickened himself with new loves and learned that drugs poison him who sickened of the beloved.

title: Sonnet 119
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Siren tears and a madding fever of errors; the benefit of ill is that ruined love rebuilt grows fairer and stronger than before.

title: Sonnet 12
author: Shakespeare
summary: Clock-and-scythe sonnet cataloguing time's ravages on nature; only breeding can brave time's scythe.

title: Sonnet 120
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Mutual trespass: the friend's past unkindness now consoles the speaker for his own; each trespass ransoms the other in reciprocal guilt and forgiveness.

title: Sonnet 121
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Defiant defense of the self ('I am that I am') against the false judgment and slander of others' eyes; identity, conscience and appearance vs reality.

title: Sonnet 122
author: Shakespeare
summary: The beloved's gift (tables/notebook) given away because memory in the brain holds love beyond all date; memory, writing, and time.

title: Sonnet 123
author: Shakespeare
summary: Defiance of Time and its scythe, vowing constancy ('I will be true') against mutability and the deceiving records of time.

title: Sonnet 124
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Love built far from accident, immune to fortune, time and politic chance; constancy of true love against mutability and fortune's wheel.

title: Sonnet 125
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Rejection of outward show and ruined 'bases for eternity' in favor of mutual, free devotion of a true soul; transience, truth, appearance vs reality.

title: Sonnet 126
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Envoi to the lovely boy: Nature's sickle-hour, her audit and quietus; mortality, time, mutability closing the fair-youth sequence.

title: Sonnet 127
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Opening Dark Lady sonnet: black is beauty's heir, mistress's raven-black eyes against cosmetic false beauty; appearance vs reality, the dark mistress.

title: Sonnet 128
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Watching the mistress play the virginals, envying the keys that kiss her hand; desire, music, the body and jealousy.

title: Sonnet 129
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: 'Th'expense of spirit in a waste of shame': the paradox of lust, savage desire, guilt and self-disgust, heaven that leads to hell.

title: Sonnet 13
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The body as a house that must not fall to decay; husbandry through an heir upholds beauty against winter and death's cold.

title: Sonnet 130
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: 'My mistress' eyes are nothing like the sun': anti-Petrarchan blazon mocking false compare; appearance vs reality and honest love.

title: Sonnet 131
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: The tyrannous cruel mistress whose black is fairest to the doting heart, black only in her deeds; desire, the unattainable beloved, the femme fatale.

title: Sonnet 132
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Her mourning black eyes pity his pain; black as beauty, love-as-religion, eyes and sight; the dark mistress as temptress.

title: Sonnet 133
author: Shakespeare
summary: The mistress has wounded both the poet and his friend; love as imprisonment, the betrayed friendship, jealousy and the femme fatale.

title: Sonnet 134
author: Shakespeare
summary: Legal/usury conceit: poet mortgaged to her will, friend bound as surety; covetous mistress, lost friendship, desire and deception.

title: Sonnet 135
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: The bawdy 'Will' pun sonnet: sexual desire and the sea receiving rain; lust, desire and the temptress.

title: Sonnet 136
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Continued 'Will' wordplay urging her soul to admit his suit; lust, desire, conscience and self-abasement.

title: Sonnet 137
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Blind love corrupts the eyes to take foul for fair, the bay where all men ride; deception, eyes/sight, appearance vs reality, the fallen woman.

title: Sonnet 138
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: 'When my love swears that she is made of truth': mutual lies and flattering self-deception in love; deception, appearance vs reality, age.

title: Sonnet 139
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Begging her not to wound by glancing aside; love-as-war (eyes that slay), her infidelity, desire and pain.

title: Sonnet 14
author: Shakespeare
summary: Astronomy-and-prognostication sonnet; the youth's eyes are constant stars from which truth and beauty are read, thriving only if he procreates.

title: Sonnet 140
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Warning the cruel mistress lest despair drive him mad to slander her; madness, desire, deception in a slanderous world.

title: Sonnet 141
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Loving against the five senses and five wits, the heart enslaved; lust as sin, the heart vs the senses, the temptress and self-and-soul.

title: Sonnet 142
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: 'Love is my sin': her profaned scarlet lips and broken bonds of love; lust, sin, adultery and the fallen woman.

title: Sonnet 143
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Housewife-and-babe simile: she chases another while the poet, her babe, cries after her; desire, neglect, the inconstant mistress.

title: Sonnet 144
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: 'Two loves I have': the fair man (better angel) and woman coloured ill (worser spirit/devil); the double, temptation, the femme fatale and good vs evil.

title: Sonnet 145
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Lighter octosyllabic lyric: 'I hate' softened to 'not you', mercy saving his life; love, mercy and the heaven/hell antithesis.

title: Sonnet 146
author: Shakespeare
summary: 'Poor soul, the centre of my sinful earth': the soul vs the dying body, contempt of the flesh, conquest of death; mortality, faith, contemptus mundi.

title: Sonnet 147
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: 'My love is as a fever': desire as disease, reason the abandoned physician, frantic madness; lust, madness, desire is death, she black as hell.

title: Sonnet 148
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Love's false eyes that cannot see aright, blinded with tears so the foul faults stay hidden; deception, eyes/sight, appearance vs reality.

title: Sonnet 149
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Self-abasing devotion to the cruel mistress, revenge upon himself, worshiping her defect; desire, self-and-soul, the unattainable beloved.

title: Sonnet 15
author: Shakespeare
summary: The world as a stage where all grows briefly perfect then decays; the poet wars with time and engrafts the youth new through verse.

title: Sonnet 150
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Her powerful might to make him love her unworthiness and what others abhor; desire, the temptress, appearance vs reality and paradox.

title: Sonnet 151
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: 'Love is too young to know what conscience is': bawdy soul-vs-flesh treason of rising and falling; lust, conscience, body and soul.

title: Sonnet 152
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Mutual perjury: her broken bed-vow and his twenty broken oaths swearing her fair; deception, broken faith, guilt and the fallen woman.

title: Sonnet 153
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Anacreontic Cupid sonnet: his brand quenched by a maid of Diana yet love's fire reignited at the mistress's eye; classical myth, fire and water.

title: Sonnet 154
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Companion Cupid sonnet: nymphs disarm the sleeping love-god, brand quenched in a well that cannot cool love; classical myth, fire and water, desire.

title: Sonnet 16
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Pivot sonnet contrasting barren rhyme with the mightier way of children to make war on bloody tyrant time.

title: Sonnet 17
author: Shakespeare
summary: Closes the procreation sequence; verse alone will be disbelieved, but a child plus the rhyme would let the youth live twice.

title: Sonnet 18
author: Shakespeare
summary: Famous 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day'; the beloved's eternal summer is immortalized in the poet's eternal lines.

title: Sonnet 19
author: Shakespeare
summary: Apostrophe to devouring time; despite time's worst the beloved will live ever young in the poet's verse.

title: Sonnet 2
author: Shakespeare
summary: Procreation sonnet imagining forty winters besieging the youth's brow; aging and decay are answered by having a child to renew beauty by succession.

title: Sonnet 20
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: The 'master-mistress' sonnet on the youth's androgynous beauty; nature created him for women's pleasure but his love is the poet's.

title: Sonnet 21
author: Shakespeare
summary: Anti-Petrarchan sonnet rejecting extravagant comparisons; the poet vows to write true love plainly rather than sell false praise.

title: Sonnet 22
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Exchanged-hearts sonnet; the lover cannot feel old while the youth is young, their hearts dwelling in each other's breasts.

title: Sonnet 23
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Tongue-tied-actor sonnet; love's strength silences speech, so the poet's books and silent looks must plead his love.

title: Sonnet 24
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Eye-as-painter conceit; the beloved's image is painted in the poet's heart, eyes as windows, though they cannot see the heart.

title: Sonnet 25
author: Shakespeare
summary: On fortune and fame; princes' favourites and warriors fall, but the poet is happy in steadfast mutual love that cannot be removed.

title: Sonnet 26
author: Shakespeare
summary: Feudal vassalage sonnet; an 'embassage' of duty to the lord of his love, hoping a guiding star will make him worthy.

title: Sonnet 27
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Weary-traveller sonnet; the body rests but the mind makes a zealous pilgrimage to the beloved, whose shadow lights black night.

title: Sonnet 28
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Continues the absence theme; day and night conspire to torture the sleepless lover with toil and grief far from the beloved.

title: Sonnet 29
author: Shakespeare
summary: 'When in disgrace with fortune'; the outcast despairing speaker is lifted like a lark by remembering the beloved's sweet love.

title: Sonnet 3
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Mirror sonnet urging the youth to look in his glass and father a child; the child as the mother's glass renews her prime against time and death.

title: Sonnet 30
author: Shakespeare
summary: 'Sessions of sweet silent thought'; memory summons past losses and dead friends, but thinking on the friend restores all sorrows.

title: Sonnet 31
author: Shakespeare
summary: The beloved as the grave where all dead loves live again; the youth holds the trophies of the poet's lost friends and all of him.

title: Sonnet 32
author: Shakespeare
summary: Anticipates the poet's death; asks the friend to keep his outdated lines for their love rather than their rhyme.

title: Sonnet 33
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: First of the 'sun' estrangement sonnets; the friend's love, like the morning sun masked by cloud, briefly shone then was hidden, yet is forgiven.

title: Sonnet 34
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Continues the storm-and-sun reproach; the friend's repentance and tears ransom the wrong done, though the wound and disgrace remain.

title: Sonnet 35
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Excuses the friend's fault ('roses have thorns'); the poet's self-corrupting advocacy makes him accessory to the sweet thief's offence.

title: Sonnet 36
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Separation sonnet; though their loves are one, the poet's guilt requires they live apart so shame does not touch the beloved.

title: Sonnet 37
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Lame-father sonnet; though made lame by fortune, the poet takes comfort and substance from the youth's worth, living by his glory.

title: Sonnet 38
author: Shakespeare
summary: The beloved as the tenth muse; he is the inexhaustible argument of the poet's verse, deserving the praise for eternal numbers.

title: Sonnet 39
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: On praising a beloved who is the better part of oneself; absence is a torment yet teaches how to make one twain through verse.

title: Sonnet 4
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Procreation sonnet using economic metaphors of usury and bequest; unused beauty is tombed with the youth, while beauty spent in offspring lives on.

title: Sonnet 40
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Betrayal sonnet; the friend has taken the poet's mistress ('gentle thief'), yet the poet forgives the robbery rather than be foes.

title: Sonnet 41
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The youth's infidelities during the poet's absence; temptation, beauty, and a betrayed two-fold troth.

title: Sonnet 42
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Friend and mistress both betray the poet; jealousy resolved by the conceit that friend and self are one.

title: Sonnet 43
author: Shakespeare
summary: In absence the poet sees the beloved best in dreams; paradox of sight, shadow, day and night.

title: Sonnet 44
author: Shakespeare
summary: Distance and absence: thought could leap to the beloved, but dull flesh of earth and water keeps the poet apart in grief.

title: Sonnet 45
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Air and fire (thought and desire) fly to the beloved in absence; melancholy and oscillating joy and sadness.

title: Sonnet 46
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A mock-legal war between eye and heart over the beloved's outward image and inward love.

title: Sonnet 47
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Eye and heart make a league; the beloved's picture and the poet's thoughts keep the absent friend present.

title: Sonnet 48
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The beloved as precious treasure that cannot be locked up; fear of theft and loss in love.

title: Sonnet 49
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Anticipating the time the beloved's love will be audited and withdrawn; self-abasement and unrequited fear.

title: Sonnet 5
author: Shakespeare
summary: Time leads summer to hideous winter; distilling flowers preserves their substance, an argument for preserving beauty through procreation.

title: Sonnet 50
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A weary journey away from the friend; the plodding horse and the rider's grief of absence.

title: Sonnet 51
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Excusing the slow horse when riding away, but desire would outrun the wind returning to the beloved.

title: Sonnet 52
author: Shakespeare
summary: The beloved as locked-up treasure made precious by rare access; seldom pleasure like feasts and jewels.

title: Sonnet 53
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The beloved's substance casts all shadows; Adonis and Helen are mere imitations; beauty and constancy.

title: Sonnet 54
author: Shakespeare
summary: Beauty made deeper by truth; the rose versus the scentless canker bloom; verse distills the youth's truth.

title: Sonnet 55
author: Shakespeare
summary: Not marble nor gilded monuments outlive this rhyme; immortality through verse against war, time, and oblivion.

title: Sonnet 56
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: An appeal to renew love's force after absence; appetite, the parting ocean, and winter making summer sweeter.

title: Sonnet 57
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The poet as abject slave watching the clock for the beloved; jealous thought suppressed in love's foolish devotion.

title: Sonnet 58
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The poet as bound vassal who must endure the beloved's liberty and absence; waiting is hell without blame.

title: Sonnet 59
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: If nothing is new, the cyclic return of all things; the wish to see the beloved's image in antique books of the past.

title: Sonnet 6
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Continues the distillation argument; breed another self before winter deface beauty so death cannot make worms thine heir.

title: Sonnet 60
author: Shakespeare
summary: Minutes like waves hastening to their end; time's scythe destroys beauty, but verse shall stand against his cruel hand.

title: Sonnet 61
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Sleepless nights haunted by the beloved's image; jealousy and the watchman's love while the friend wakes elsewhere.

title: Sonnet 62
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Sin of self-love confronted by the aging face in the glass; identity dissolves into love of the youth.

title: Sonnet 63
author: Shakespeare
summary: Fortifying against age's cruel knife; the youth's beauty kept alive in black lines despite time's decay.

title: Sonnet 64
author: Shakespeare
summary: Time's defacing of towers, brass, and the contending sea and shore; ruin teaches that time will take the beloved away.

title: Sonnet 65
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Mortality oversways brass, stone, earth, sea; only the miracle of black ink keeps the beloved's beauty bright.

title: Sonnet 66
author: Shakespeare
summary: Weary catalogue of social injustice and corruption; the poet cries for death but stays for love.

title: Sonnet 67
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Why should the youth live amid infection and false art; his true rose set against painted counterfeits of beauty.

title: Sonnet 68
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The youth's cheek as a map of antique days, true beauty without cosmetic art and golden wigs of the dead.

title: Sonnet 69
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: The youth's outward beauty praised, but tongues impugn his mind; appearance versus the rank smell of his deeds.

title: Sonnet 7
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The sun's daily rise and decline as emblem of youth and age; the youth must get a son to be looked on in his decline.

title: Sonnet 70
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Slander as the ornament of beauty; the youth defended as pure prime assailed by envy and suspicion.

title: Sonnet 71
author: Shakespeare
summary: No longer mourn for me when I am dead; the surly bell, worms, and the wish to be forgotten in death.

title: Sonnet 72
author: Shakespeare
summary: Begging to be forgotten after death lest love speak a virtuous lie; self-shaming and the buried name.

title: Sonnet 73
author: Shakespeare
summary: Autumn boughs, twilight, and dying fire as emblems of aging and approaching death, strengthening love.

title: Sonnet 74
author: Shakespeare
summary: Death's fell arrest carries off the body, but the spirit and the line remain with the beloved; verse as memorial.

title: Sonnet 75
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The beloved as food to life; the miser's alternating feast and famine, gluttony and starvation in love.

title: Sonnet 76
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Why the poet's verse never varies; he always writes of one love, dressing old words new, like the daily sun.

title: Sonnet 77
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Glass, dial, and blank book teach the lessons of mortality, time's thievish progress, and memory committed to writing.

title: Sonnet 78
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The rival-poet sequence begins; alien pens use the beloved as muse, but the poet claims him as all his art.

title: Sonnet 79
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The poet's muse decayed as a worthier rival pen takes his place; the rival only repays what the beloved already owns.

title: Sonnet 8
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Music-and-harmony sonnet; the concord of strings as sire, child and mother argues that the single life proves none.

title: Sonnet 80
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The poet faints before a better spirit who praises the beloved; the rival's tall ship versus his saucy little barque on the ocean of worth.

title: Sonnet 81
author: Shakespeare
summary: The poet vows his verse will be the beloved's monument, granting immortality through poetry even as the poet himself dies.

title: Sonnet 82
author: Shakespeare
summary: Rival-poet sonnet contrasting other writers' rhetorical 'painting' with the speaker's plain true praise of the fair youth.

title: Sonnet 83
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: The poet defends his silence as truer praise than rival poets', insisting the youth's beauty exceeds all verse.

title: Sonnet 84
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: On the inexpressibility of the youth's beauty: the best praise is simply that 'you alone are you', and excess praise is a curse.

title: Sonnet 85
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The tongue-tied muse stays silent while rivals write golden praise; the speaker loves in dumb thought rather than words.

title: Sonnet 86
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Climax of the rival-poet sequence: the rival's proud verse and 'familiar ghost' did not silence the speaker; only the youth's favour to the rival did.

title: Sonnet 87
author: Shakespeare
summary: 'Farewell' sonnet of estrangement and loss, the love figured as a dream of kingship dissolved on waking.

title: Sonnet 88
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Self-abnegating love: the speaker will fight against himself and bear all wrong to vindicate the beloved who has wronged him.

title: Sonnet 89
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The speaker will disgrace himself and estrange himself to justify the beloved's rejection, vowing to hate whom the beloved hates.

title: Sonnet 9
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Procreation sonnet; to die issueless makes the world a weeping widow, and unused beauty is self-murderous waste.

title: Sonnet 90
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Begging the beloved to abandon him now, at fortune's worst, so all other griefs pale beside the loss of love.

title: Sonnet 91
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Catalogue of men's prides (birth, wealth, hawks, horses) all surpassed by the beloved's love, yet shadowed by fear of its loss.

title: Sonnet 92
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: The speaker is secured by the beloved's love unto death, yet ends fearing hidden falsehood he cannot know.

title: Sonnet 93
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: The deceived-husband sonnet: the beloved's sweet face may mask a false heart, likened to Eve's apple of fair appearance and hidden corruption.

title: Sonnet 94
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: On those who have power to hurt but withhold it; the summer flower festering warns that sweetest things turn sourest by their deeds.

title: Sonnet 95
author: Shakespeare
summary: Beauty veils sin like a canker in the fragrant rose; the youth's loveliness makes shame sweet, but the knife ill used loses its edge.

title: Sonnet 96
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: The youth turns faults to graces; the wolf-in-lamb image warns of his power to lead astray, yet the speaker guards his good name.

title: Sonnet 97
author: Shakespeare
summary: Absence from the beloved felt as winter though it was autumn; the teeming season seems barren and the birds mute without him.

title: Sonnet 98
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Absent in spring amid April's flowers and birdsong, the speaker finds them mere shadows of the beloved and feels it still winter.

title: Sonnet 99
author: Shakespeare
summary: The flowers (violet, lily, roses) are charged with stealing their sweetness and colour from the beloved; an unusual 15-line sonnet.

title: Sonnet-To Science
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A sonnet attacking science as a vulture that preys on the poet's heart, banishing the mythological imagination (Diana, the Naiad, the Hamadryad) and dull realities against poetic vision.

title: Sonnets
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Shakespeare's 154 sonnets. The Fair Youth sequence urges procreation, then immortalizes the beloved's beauty against time and decay through the poet's own eternal verse; the later Dark Lady sonnets turn to desire, jealousy and disillusion. Recurrent notes are love and beauty, the ravages of time, appearance versus reality, and art as a defense against mortality.

title: Soon Shall the Winter’s Foil Be Here
author: Whitman
summary: Anticipates spring melting winter's icy ligatures, a thousand forms rising from dead clods as the annual play returns.

title: Sounds of the Winter
author: Whitman
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A wintry pastoral of cheerful rural sounds, the old man among them insisting he has not given out yet but keeps up the lilt from his snowy hairs.

title: Spain, 1873-74
author: Whitman
cluster: Ruins the Abbey · Sic Transit Gloria Mundi · Ubi Sunt
summary: A free-verse political ode hailing Freedom rising from feudal European ruins, addressed maternally to Columbia; themes of liberty, revolution and the ruins of the old order.

title: Sparkles from the Wheel
author: Whitman
summary: City vignette of a knife-grinder at his wheel throwing golden sparkles, the poet a floating phantom absorbed in the scene; the city, the common man, the wheel, and perception.

title: Spirit That Form’d This Scene
author: Whitman
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A free-verse lyric set in Platte Canyon defending the poet's wild, ruleless art by analogy to savage Nature; themes of nature vs civilization and the artist.

title: Spirit Whose Work Is Done (Washington City, 1865)
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Invocation to the departing spirit of war to bequeath its rage and pulses to the poet's chants as the soldiers return home and the conflict closes.

title: Spirits of the Dead
author: Poe
summary: A graveyard lyric in which the solitary soul is surrounded in death by the spirits of the dead, amid night, stars and an oppressive supernatural mystery.

title: Spontaneous Me
author: Whitman
summary: Catalogue of natural and bodily eroticism, love-juice and procreation matched to the chastity of nature; desire, the body, nature, innocence.

title: Starting from Paumanok
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Long programmatic chant proclaiming the new American bard of democracy, body and soul, sex, religion and comradeship across the continent; sprawling catalogue free verse.

title: Still Though the One I Sing
author: Whitman
summary: Dedicates the one (of contradictions) to Nationality while leaving in him the quenchless fire of revolt; democracy, the rebel, identity.

title: Stronger Lessons
author: Whitman
summary: Asks whether one has learned the stronger lessons from those who reject and oppose rather than admire one.

title: THE COMEDY OF ERRORS
author: Shakespeare
summary: Farcical Plautine comedy of two sets of identical twins separated at sea, producing a cascade of mistaken identity in Ephesus before family reunion. Central themes: identity, appearance vs reality, marriage, the comic recovery of lost kin.

title: THE FIRST PART OF THE CONTENTION - (2 HENRY VI)
author: Shakespeare
summary: History play dramatizing the disintegration of weak King Henry VI's realm: the fall of Duke Humphrey, the rise of York's claim, Queen Margaret's intrigues, and Jack Cade's bloody populist rebellion. Themes of kingship and legitimacy, ambition, order vs chaos, and civil war.

title: THE HISTORY OF KING LEAR - THE QUARTO TEXT
author: Shakespeare
summary: The Quarto text of Shakespeare's great tragedy: an aged king divides his kingdom by flattery, is cast out into the storm by ungrateful daughters, and descends into madness; themes of kingship, filial ingratitude, madness, nature, and order versus chaos.

title: THE MERCHANT OF VENICE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A tragicomedy in which the merchant Antonio borrows from the Jewish moneylender Shylock on a bond of a pound of flesh; it turns on the conflict of justice and mercy, the casket-test courtship of Portia, and the trial scene resolved by Portia disguised as a lawyer.

title: THE MERRY WIVES OF WINDSOR
author: Shakespeare
summary: A middle-class citizen comedy set in Windsor in which Falstaff's attempts to seduce two married women are turned against him by the wives' ingenious tricks; a farce of disguise, jealousy, and bourgeois domestic life.

title: THE RAPE OF LUCRECE
author: Shakespeare
summary: Tragic narrative poem in rhyme royal: Tarquin's rape of the chaste Roman matron Lucrece, her grief and suicide, and the political revolution it triggers. Central themes: lust, honour and chastity, guilt, justice and the fall of tyranny.

title: THE TAMING OF THE SHREW
author: Shakespeare
summary: Robust early Shakespearean comedy verging on farce: Petruccio woos and 'tames' the shrewish Katherine while disguised suitors compete for Bianca, framed by the Christopher Sly induction that explores persuasion, appearance vs reality, and the play-within-the-play.

title: THE TEMPEST
author: Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's late romance on the magician Prospero, exiled duke who raises a storm to bring his usurpers to his island, tests the lovers Ferdinand and Miranda, and finally forgives; central are magic and the supernatural, usurpation, forgiveness, nature versus civilization, and art.

title: THE TRAGEDY OF KING LEAR - THE FOLIO TEXT
author: Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's great tragedy in blank verse on the aged King Lear who divides his kingdom by flattery, descends into madness and the storm, and is broken by filial ingratitude; central are kingship, the natural order, madness, suffering, and the question of justice in a pitiless world.

title: THE TWO GENTLEMEN OF VERONA
author: Shakespeare
summary: Early Shakespearean romantic comedy in which the friends Valentine and Proteus both fall for Silvia; centres on the conflicting claims of love and friendship, fidelity vs betrayal, courtly love and disguise (Julia following Proteus dressed as a boy).

title: THE TWO NOBLE KINSMEN
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late tragicomic romance (with Fletcher) from Chaucer's Knight's Tale, in which kinsmen Palamon and Arcite, sworn friends, fall in love with Emilia and fight to the death for her; themes are the conflict of love and friendship, fortune's paradoxes, and chivalric ritual.

title: THE WINTER’S TALE
author: Shakespeare
summary: A late dramatic romance in which Leontes' irrational jealousy destroys his family, followed across sixteen years by pastoral renewal and the wondrous restoration of the lost daughter Perdita and the statue-like Hermione; its themes are jealousy, repentance, time, and redemptive grace.

title: TIMON OF ATHENS
author: Shakespeare
summary: A bitter, schematic tragedy/satire in which the lavishly generous Timon, abandoned by flattering friends once his wealth fails, turns misanthrope and curses humanity from the wilderness; themes of money, false friendship, ingratitude and misanthropy.

title: TITUS ANDRONICUS
author: Shakespeare
summary: Bloody Senecan revenge tragedy set in late Rome: the cycle of mutilation, rape and cannibalistic vengeance between Titus and Tamora. Central themes: revenge, the grotesque and horror, justice and barbarism.

title: TROILUS AND CRESSIDA
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Order vs Chaos · Historical Novel · Fanaticism
summary: A bitter, philosophical play set during the Trojan War that deflates heroic ideals and dramatizes the betrayal of love by Cressida; a sardonic anatomy of war, lust, time and the frailty of human value.

title: TWELFTH NIGHT
author: Shakespeare
summary: A festive romantic comedy of shipwreck, twins, cross-dressing disguise and mistaken identity in Illyria, where tangled love, music and folly resolve in marriage; a comedy turning on appearance versus reality.

title: Tamerlane
author: Poe
summary: A dying conqueror's deathbed confession to a friar, lamenting how ambition and pride for the throne of Samarcand cost him his youthful love; a meditation on ambition, lost love and worldly glory's emptiness.

title: Tears
author: Whitman
summary: A nocturnal shore lyric of grief: a ghostly figure weeping unloosed tears like a storm at night; free-verse on grief, the sea, night and hidden sorrow.

title: Tests
author: Whitman
summary: Brief free-verse fragment asserting that the soul's inner judgments, not outer authorities or traditions, are the true tests of all things.

title: Thanks in Old Age
author: Whitman
summary: A thanksgiving in old age for life, memories, family, readers and brave men, given as a returning soldier's grateful thanks.

title: That Music Always Round Me
author: Whitman
summary: The speaker awakens to the unceasing cosmic chorus of voices and instruments, hearing in it exquisite meanings and beginning to know the performers.

title: That Shadow My Likeness
author: Whitman
summary: Poet doubts whether the worldly shadow-self is really him, but never doubts his identity among lovers and songs; identity, self and soul, the double.

title: The Angel of the Odd
author: Poe
summary: A drunken skeptic is plagued by a grotesque liquor-cask spirit who orchestrates a cascade of absurd accidents to punish his disbelief in the improbable; a comic extravaganza on chance and the grotesque.

title: The Artilleryman’s Vision
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A veteran at home is seized by a midnight vision of battle, hearing the missiles and feeling the old mad joy; war-trauma, memory and the haunting persistence of combat.

title: The Assignation
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A Byronic stranger in Venice and the married Marchesa Aphrodite share a forbidden love that ends in their simultaneous death by poison at the appointed hour; a tale of love-as-religion, doomed passion and aestheticism.

title: The Ballad of Reading Gaol
author: Wilde
summary: A ballad recounting the execution of a condemned guardsman, meditating on guilt, mercy, the cruelty of prison and Man's justice, and the redemptive figure of Christ, framed by the refrain that each man kills the thing he loves.

title: The Balloon-Hoax
author: Poe
summary: A fabricated newspaper account of the first transatlantic balloon crossing, presented as fact; a hoax celebrating science, technology and the credulity of the age.

title: The Base of All Metaphysics
author: Whitman
summary: Professor's farewell declaring that beneath Greek and Germanic philosophy and Christ lies 'the dear love of man for his comrade'; comradeship as the ground of metaphysics.

title: The Bells
author: Poe
summary: An onomatopoeic lyric tracing the bells of life from merry sledge-bells through wedding-bells to alarm-bells and finally the funereal iron tolling of death; a sonic meditation on time, mutability and mortality.

title: The Birthday of the Infanta
author: Wilde
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: At the Spanish court a deformed dwarf, loved by no one, dances for the Infanta until a mirror reveals his ugliness and his heart breaks; a tragic tale of cruelty, beauty versus ugliness, and the grotesque.

title: The Black Cat
author: Poe
summary: A condemned narrator confesses how alcohol and the spirit of perverseness led him to mutilate and hang his cat and murder his wife, his guilt betrayed by a second cat; a tale of guilt, madness and the grotesque.

title: The Bravest Soldiers
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield

title: The Business Man
author: Poe
summary: A self-styled methodical 'man of business' satirizes commercial society by pursuing a series of petty, swindling 'methodical' trades; a satire of money-grubbing and bourgeois respectability.

title: The Calming Thought of All
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Amid changing theologies and philosophies, the earth's silent vital laws continue, a calming natural order.

title: The Canterville Ghost
author: Wilde
summary: A comic-gothic story parodying the haunted-house tale: a centuries-old English ghost is defeated by an unflappable, materialist American family, yet finds release through a child's pity and prayer, ending in genuine grace, forgiveness and the recurrent bloodstain motif.

title: The Cask of Amontillado
author: Poe
summary: A first-person tale of premeditated revenge in which Montresor lures the wine-loving Fortunato into the catacombs during carnival and walls him up alive; its central matter is revenge, deception, and dramatic irony.

title: The Centenarian’s Story
author: Whitman
summary: A narrative poem in which a Revolutionary War centenarian recalls Washington's defeat at Brooklyn and the slaughter of the young brigade; war, sacrifice, memory and national continuity.

title: The City Dead-House
author: Whitman
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Meditation on the unclaimed corpse of a dead prostitute as a ruined yet immortal 'house,' tenement of a soul; death, the body, compassion, and the outcast.

title: The City in the Sea
author: Poe
summary: A visionary lyric depicting a doomed city of the dead where Death reigns enthroned among ruined towers before the whole town sinks into the sea; its themes are mortality, ruin, and apocalyptic decay.

title: The Coliseum
author: Poe
cluster: Ruins the Abbey · Sic Transit Gloria Mundi · Ubi Sunt
summary: A meditative blank-verse poem on the ruins of the Roman Coliseum that turns the fallen monument into a lesson on the passing of glory and the enduring power of memory; an ubi sunt / sic transit reflection.

title: The Colloquy of Monos and Una
author: Poe
summary: A dialogue between two reunited souls after death describing the sensations of dying and bodily decay, framed by a critique of mechanical progress and modern civilization.

title: The Commonplace
author: Whitman
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Whitman sings the cheap, common, democratic wisdom of everyday life and the open air, with an appended dark catalogue probing the place of evil in earth's scheme.

title: The Conqueror Worm
author: Poe
summary: A theatrum-mundi lyric in which human life is staged as a tragedy watched by weeping angels, its hero the devouring Worm; a despairing allegory of mortality, sin, and madness.

title: The Conversation of Eiros and Charmion
author: Poe
summary: A dialogue of disembodied souls recounting the destruction of the Earth by a comet that burned away the atmosphere; an apocalyptic tale of cosmic annihilation and the afterlife.

title: The Critic as Artist
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Critical dialogue arguing that criticism is itself a creative art; a sustained aesthetic meditation on beauty, imagination, contemplation and the artist and society.

title: The Dalliance of the Eagles
author: Whitman
summary: On a river walk the poet witnesses two eagles mating in mid-air, a fierce gyrating wheel then parting; a free-verse lyric on birds, nature, desire and motion.

title: The Dead Emperor
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: America bends in mourning for a dead Emperor, condoling less the crown than a good old man and patriot.

title: The Dead Tenor
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Elegy for an operatic tenor whose singing voice taught the poet, his memory dropped like an autumn leaf into the grave.

title: The Decay of Lying
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Aesthetic critical dialogue arguing art over nature, lying as art, and that life imitates art; a manifesto of art for art's sake rich in paradox and epigram.

title: The Devil in the Belfry
author: Poe
summary: A comic satire in which a devilish stranger invades an orderly clockwork Dutch borough and overturns its obsession with time and routine; a burlesque of bourgeois order turned upside down.

title: The Devoted Friend
author: Wilde
summary: A satirical fable in which a rich Miller exploits and finally causes the death of little Hans while endlessly preaching the virtues of 'true friendship', mocking hypocrisy and false friendship.

title: The Dismantled Ship
author: Whitman
summary: An old battered dismasted ship, after all its voyages, lies rusting and mouldering in a nameless bay, an image of aged decline.

title: The Domain of Arnheim
author: Poe
summary: A reflective tale-essay on landscape gardening as the highest art, in which a wealthy aesthete builds an earthly paradise; its matter is beauty, the sublime, and the artist's creation of an ideal garden.

title: The Duc de L'omelette
author: Poe
cluster: Temptation · Good vs Evil · Serpent Snake
summary: A flippant comic tale in which a dandified Duc dies of gourmandise, finds himself before the Devil in Hell, and wins his soul back at cards; a satire of foppery and a playful treatment of damnation.

title: The Duchess of Padua
author: Wilde
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: Wilde's second play, a five-act blank-verse revenge tragedy set in Renaissance Padua; Guido is driven to avenge his murdered father against the tyrannical Duke, falls into transgressive love with the Duchess Beatrice, and the pair die together amid guilt, sin and redemption. Central themes: revenge, forbidden love, guilt and mercy, the corrupt tyrant.

title: The Dying Veteran
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A Revolutionary War veteran on his deathbed cries to return to his old battle-life, rejecting the present age of peace.

title: The Facts in the Case of M. Valdemar
author: Poe
summary: A pseudo-scientific horror tale in which a dying man is mesmerized at the point of death and held suspended for months until his sudden, grotesque dissolution; themes of death, the uncanny, and bodily decay.

title: The Fall of the House of Usher
author: Poe
summary: A gothic tale of the doomed twins Roderick and Madeline Usher, premature burial, hereditary madness and the literal collapse of their decaying house; a study in terror, the double, and the uncanny.

title: The First Dandelion
author: Whitman
summary: A spring nature lyric celebrating the season's first dandelion as innocent and renewing after winter.

title: The Fisherman and his Soul
author: Wilde
summary: A fairy tale in which a young fisherman cuts away his shadow-soul to wed a mermaid; the disembodied, heartless Soul becomes his tempting double, dramatizing desire versus soul, body versus spirit, and the sea as the realm of pagan love against the Priest's Christian condemnation.

title: The Forest Reverie
author: Poe
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: A lyric likening the felling of a primeval wood to the wasting of love, from whose grief spring 'the rare and radiant flowers of song'; nature imagery turned to loss redeemed by poetry.

title: The Gold-Bug
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A tale of ratiocination in which Legrand decodes a pirate's cryptogram to unearth Captain Kidd's buried treasure; a detective-style story driven by cipher-breaking, gold, and analytic reasoning.

title: The Happiest Day
author: Poe
cluster: Vanitas · Contemptus Mundi · Vanity of Worldly Things
summary: Early lyric of disillusionment in which the speaker renounces past hopes of pride and power, dwelling on the transience of youth and the soul-destroying alloy hidden in joy.

title: The Happy Prince
author: Wilde
summary: Fairy-tale allegory of charity and self-sacrifice: a gilded statue and a swallow give away gold and jewels to the city's poor and are redeemed as the two most precious things by God.

title: The Haunted Palace
author: Poe
summary: Allegorical poem in which a once-radiant palace (the mind of monarch Thought) falls to evil and madness, dramatizing decay, mutability and the fall from a golden past.

title: The Imp of the Perverse
author: Poe
summary: Essay-tale on the self-destructive impulse to act against one's own interest; a murderer's compulsion to confess illustrates guilt, conscience and perverse human nature.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest
author: Wilde
summary: Farcical comedy of manners turning on Bunburying/double identities, courtship and marriage, and a sustained satire of late-Victorian London society.

title: The Island of the Fay
author: Poe
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Meditative prose-poem on solitude and natural scenery in which a solitary dreamer watches a fairy circle an island, her vanishing shadow allegorizing the cycle of life and death.

title: The Lake -- To--
author: Poe
cluster: Ode · Nature vs Civilization · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Lyric of youthful solitude at a wild lake whose nocturnal terror becomes a tremulous delight, mingling death, imagination and a private Eden of the lone soul.

title: The Landscape Garden
author: Poe
summary: Aesthetic tale-essay in which the immensely wealthy poet Ellison devotes his fortune to landscape-gardening as the supreme art, theorizing beauty, nature and the artist's creation of an intermediate Nature between man and God.

title: The Last Invocation
author: Whitman
summary: Gentle prayer for the soul at death to be wafted noiselessly from the fortressed house of the body, unlocking the doors of mortal flesh and love.

title: The Literary Life of Thingum Bob, Esq
author: Poe
summary: Comic mock-autobiography satirizing the corruption, puffery and vanity of the American literary marketplace through the rise of a fatuous, self-glorifying editor.

title: The Lost Tools of Learning
author: Sayers
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: In this 1947 Oxford lecture Sayers contends that modern schooling teaches a multitude of "subjects" but fails to teach children how to think, leaving them defenceless against propaganda, advertising and sloppy argument. Her remedy is to revive the medieval Trivium—Grammar, Dialectic and Rhetoric—as the true tools of learning, matching each to a natural stage of the child's development (the Poll-parrot, the Pert and the Poetic ages). The sole end of education, she insists, is to teach people how to learn for themselves, so that any subject becomes an open door.

title: The Man That Was Used Up
author: Poe
summary: Grotesque satire in which a celebrated war-hero general proves to be a literal assemblage of manufactured prosthetics, mocking the age's faith in mechanical progress and hollow public reputation.

title: The Man of the Crowd
author: Poe
summary: A convalescent narrator obsessively follows an enigmatic old man through nocturnal London, finding in his refusal to be alone the unreadable type and genius of deep crime amid the modern crowd.

title: The Masque of the Red Death
author: Poe
summary: Allegory in which Prince Prospero's sealed revel cannot escape the plague: the masked Red Death enters the seven chambers as the ebony clock tolls, asserting Death's illimitable dominion.

title: The Mind of the Maker
author: Sayers
summary: Writing not as an apologist but as a professional writer, Sayers argues that the Christian creeds' statements about God the Creator are, when tested against direct experience, an exact description of the human creative mind. Every act of making is a threefold, Trinitarian structure—the Creative Idea (the Father), the Creative Energy or Activity incarnate in matter (the Word), and the Creative Power responding in the reader's soul (the Spirit)—three distinct "Persons" that are yet one work. From this analogy she illuminates free will, miracle, the problem of evil, self-expression, and the worth of work, and she diagnoses a modern age that mistakes life for a "problem" to be solved rather than a creation to be made.

title: The Model Millionaire
author: Wilde
summary: Short story in which a beggar-model is secretly a millionaire who rewards a poor lover's charity, satirising money, appearance versus reality and the artist's world.

title: The Murders in the Rue Morgue
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: The foundational tale of ratiocination in which C. Auguste Dupin solves a baffling Parisian double murder through analytical deduction, inaugurating modern detective fiction.

title: The Mystery of Marie Roget
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A Dupin ratiocinative tale reconstructing the murder of a young Parisian shop-girl (mirroring the real Mary Rogers case) through probability, newspaper analysis, and armchair detection.

title: The Mystic Trumpeter
author: Whitman
summary: An unseen ghostly trumpeter conjures in turn the feudal past, love, war, despair, and finally a redeemed future of universal joy; music as visionary power.

title: The Narrative of A. Gordon Pym (Raven Edition)
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: A first-person sea-voyage adventure novel of stowaway, mutiny, shipwreck, starvation, cannibalism and a southward quest ending in an apocalyptic Antarctic vision of a white shrouded figure and a silent cataract.

title: The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket
author: Poe
cluster: Night Journey Vision · Katabasis Descent · Quest Hero
summary: Poe's only completed novel: a frame-tale sea adventure of stowaway, mutiny, shipwreck, starvation, cannibalism and a hallucinatory voyage to a mysterious all-white Antarctic region. Central themes are terror, the quest into the unknown, and the dissolution of identity at the white limit of the world.

title: The Nightingale and the Rose
author: Wilde
summary: A nightingale gives her heart's blood to make a red rose for love, only for the gift to be scorned; a fairy tale on self-sacrifice, the worth of love versus utility, and white turning to red.

title: The Ox-Tamer
author: Whitman
summary: Pastoral portrait of an illiterate farmer who tames wild oxen by love; celebrates the common man, animals and rural life over books.

title: The Pallid Wreath
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: An elegiac lyric on memory and grief: a withered funeral wreath kept hanging because the dead friend remains vivid and unfaded in remembrance.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Wilde
summary: Gothic novel of aestheticism in which a Faustian wish keeps Dorian beautiful while a hidden portrait bears the corruption of his soul, exploring beauty, sin, the double, and conscience.

title: The Portrait of Mr. W. H.
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: A story-essay defending the Willie Hughes theory of Shakespeare's Sonnets, in which a forged portrait, aesthetic faith, and male friendship lead two men to die for a literary idea.

title: The Prairie States
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Compact paean to the prairie states as a new modern garden of creation, a teeming democratic paradise justifying the past.

title: The Prairie-Grass Dividing
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Demand for free, sunlit, audacious companionship modeled on the open prairie-grass; nature, grass, the common man, comradeship and democratic self-reliance.

title: The Raven
author: Poe
summary: Poe's signature narrative poem: a bereaved lover, mourning the lost Lenore at midnight, is visited by a talking raven whose 'Nevermore' deepens his grief into despair. Themes of mortality, grief, memory and irrational dread.

title: The Remarkable Rocket
author: Wilde
summary: A satirical fairy tale skewering vanity and self-importance: a pompous rocket convinced of his own greatness fizzles unseen in a ditch, a comedy of pride and self-delusion.

title: The Return of the Heroes
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Harvest hymn celebrating the disbanding Union armies turning from war to the life-giving labor of the fertile American earth; nature, abundance, and the cost of war recalled.

title: The Runner
author: Whitman
summary: A four-line free-verse vignette of a lean, sinewy athlete in motion; an imagistic celebration of the healthy body and bodily energy.

title: The Selfish Giant
author: Wilde
cluster: Bible · Sin and the Fall · Fall from Innocence
summary: A Christian fairy-tale allegory of redemption: a giant's selfishness brings perpetual winter to his garden until he welcomes the children and the Christ-child leads him to Paradise.

title: The Ship Starting
author: Whitman
summary: Imagistic vignette of a ship setting out on the unbounded sea with all sails spread; the sea, the journey, voyage as the open road.

title: The Singer in the Prison
author: Whitman
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · Bread and Wine Eucharist
summary: A lady sings a redeeming hymn to convicts about the imprisoned soul freed by the pardoner death; music, sin, grace, the body, and death as deliverance.

title: The Sleeper
author: Poe
summary: A nocturnal lyric meditating on a beautiful dead (or deathly sleeping) woman, Irene, beneath the mystic moon; her sleep merges with the grave. Themes of death, the dead beloved, sleep and melancholy.

title: The Sleepers
author: Whitman
summary: Long dream-journey through the night in which the wandering soul merges with all sleepers and dreamers; death, night and sleep level and reconcile humanity.

title: The Sobbing of the Bells (Midnight, Sept. 19-20, 1881)
author: Whitman
summary: A brief free-verse elegy on the tolling bells announcing President Garfield's death and the nation's grief; themes of death, bells, the nation and mourning.

title: The Soul of Man under Socialism
author: Wilde
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · Common Man
summary: Political-aesthetic essay arguing that abolishing private property frees a true Individualism, attacking poverty, charity, authority and public opinion, and championing the artist's autonomy from society.

title: The Sphinx
author: Poe
summary: A short tale set during a cholera epidemic in which the narrator, sick with dread, mistakes a tiny death's-head moth on a windowpane for a monstrous distant apparition; a parable of misjudged proximity and the mind's terror. Themes of terror, omens, appearance vs reality.

title: The Sphinx
author: Wilde
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Wilde's decadent narrative poem in which a student addresses an immortal Egyptian Sphinx, conjuring her ancient lovers and exotic gods amid lust, decay and ruin, before recoiling toward his crucifix at the close.

title: The Sphinx Without a Secret
author: Wilde
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Short story of an enigmatic woman whose 'mystery' proves empty; a Sphinx without a secret, exploring appearance versus reality, secrecy and unrequited love.

title: The Star-Child
author: Wilde
summary: A fairy tale of a beautiful but proud and cruel foundling who, punished with ugliness for denying his beggar mother, undergoes a penitential quest of humility and charity, is restored, and redeemed in an explicitly Christ-toned arc of fall, suffering and redemption.

title: The System of Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether
author: Poe
summary: A satirical horror-comedy: a visitor to a French madhouse discovers the lunatics have overthrown their keepers and taken over the asylum. Themes of madness, the world upside down, and appearance vs reality.

title: The Tell-Tale Heart
author: Poe
summary: A first-person tale of a mad narrator who murders an old man over his 'vulture eye', dismembers the body, then is undone by the imagined beating of the dead man's heart. Themes of madness, guilt, conscience and terror.

title: The Thousand-And-Second Tale of Scheherazade
author: Poe
summary: A satirical frame-tale extending the Arabian Nights: Scheherazade tells of Sindbad's encounters with modern marvels of science, which the incredulous king finds too improbable, and has her executed. Themes of truth stranger than fiction, satire and wonder.

title: The Torch
author: Whitman
summary: Imagist miniature of Northwest fishermen spearing salmon by torchlight at night on a black lake; pure nocturnal image of fire on water.

title: The Truth of Masks
author: Wilde
cluster: Artist and Society · Truth · Regency Georgian England
summary: Wilde's critical essay on Shakespeare's use of costume and illusion, arguing that archaeological accuracy is a method of artistic illusion and ending on the paradox that the truths of metaphysics are the truths of masks.

title: The Unexpress’d
author: Whitman
summary: After all the world's poetry from Homer to Shakespeare, the poet wonders whether the best still remains unexpressed and lacking, a topos of inexpressibility.

title: The United States to Old World Critics
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: America answers European critics by pointing to its concrete daily building of a vast perpetual edifice rising to the stars.

title: The Unparalleled Adventures of one Hans Pfaall
author: Poe
summary: A proto-science-fiction hoax-tale: a bankrupt Rotterdam bellows-mender escapes his debts by ballooning to the Moon, narrated with pseudo-scientific detail. Themes of the quest, the journey, satire and wonder.

title: The Valley of Unrest
author: Poe
summary: A short lyric on a once-peaceful dell, now restless and weeping over a nameless grave after its people went to the wars. Themes of death, mutability, melancholy and a haunted landscape.

title: The Village Street
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A melancholic narrative lyric: a nocturnal walk with a scornful maiden ends in parting and lifelong heartbreak, the once-pleasant elms now whispering mad, discordant melodies. Themes of lost love, melancholy and memory.

title: The Voice of the Rain
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: The rain answers the poet as the 'Poem of Earth', an eternal cycle of rising and returning likened to song.

title: The Wallabout Martyrs
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Elegy for Revolutionary War prison-ship dead, ranked above classical heroes as the foundation stones of America.

title: The World below the Brine
author: Whitman
summary: A catalogue of the strange life of the ocean floor and its passions and wars, paralleling change between spheres of being; free-verse lyric on the sea, nature and metempsychosis.

title: The Wound Dresser: A Series of Letters Written from the Hospitals in Washington during the War of the Rebellion
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Whitman's Civil War letters and hospital memoranda from Washington DC, recording his nursing of wounded and dying soldiers and the human cost of the war. The text centers on death, suffering, comradeship, and the dignity of the common soldier, written in plain epistolary autobiographical prose.

title: The Wound-Dresser
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: An old man recalls tending the wounded and dying in army hospitals, dressing terrible wounds with impassive hand and burning heart; compassion, suffering and the human cost of war.

title: The Young King
author: Wilde
summary: A fairy-tale allegory in which a beauty-loving young king, taught by three dreams of the suffering behind his coronation finery, renounces luxury and is crowned by divine light as a Christ-like figure.

title: There Was a Child Went Forth
author: Whitman
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: Catalog of a child becoming everything he beholds, from lilacs and farm animals to parents and the city; identity, childhood, perception, and the merging of self and world.

title: These I Singing in Spring
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Spring-walk poem of the 'poet of comrades' gathering natural tokens (the calamus-root) for lovers; nature, love, friendship and memory of the dead in free verse.

title: Thick-Sprinkled Bunting
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse apostrophe to the American flag prophesying its supremacy over the flags of kings; themes of patriotism, democracy and the flag of man.

title: This Compost
author: Whitman
summary: Awe and terror at the earth's chemistry that grows sweet spring crops out of diseased corpses; death, decay, regeneration, nature, and resurrection of the grass.

title: This Dust Was Once the Man
author: Whitman
summary: Epitaph-quatrain for Lincoln, the gentle resolute man who saved the Union against the foulest crime in history; mortality, dust, and martyrdom.

title: This Moment Yearning and Thoughtful
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Poet imagining brethren and lovers yearning in other lands; comradeship extended into international, cosmopolitan brotherhood.

title: Thou Art the Man
author: Poe
cluster: Short Story · Concealment Hidden Identity · Justice Right and Wrong
summary: A comic detective/ratiocination tale: the narrator unmasks 'Old Charley Goodfellow' as the murderer of his friend by springing the corpse from a wine-box to cry 'Thou art the man'. Themes of detection, guilt, deception and appearance vs reality.

title: Thou Mother with Thy Equal Brood
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Prophetic ode to America as the great Mother and ship of Democracy, blending body and soul, fusing past nations and pointing to a spiritual future Union.

title: Thou Orb Aloft Full-Dazzling
author: Whitman
summary: Invocation to the October noon sun as fructifying lover, asking it to shed its ray on the poet's chants and prepare his lengthening shadows and starry nights.

title: Thought (As I sit with others at a great feast)
author: Whitman

title: Thought (Of Equality)
author: Whitman
