title: Thought (Of justice)
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom

title: Thought (Of obedience, faith, adhesiveness)
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom

title: Thought
author: Whitman
summary: At a feast a spectral vision of a shipwreck at sea (the steamship Arctic) prompts the anguished question whether souls are drowned and matter alone triumphant.

title: Thought
author: Whitman
cluster: Vanitas · Contemptus Mundi · Vanity of Worldly Things
summary: Satiric meditation on people of high position whose attainments sink away, mocking false realities and rotten core happiness; vanitas, the self, and critique of society.

title: Thoughts (Of public opinion)
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom

title: Thoughts (Of these years I sing)
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse catalogue on public opinion, the fall of corrupt officials and the rise of the democratic New World; themes of democracy and the common man.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A two-part free-verse meditation on America's birth-pangs, the war's price and the westward seeds of the future; themes of democracy, the West and transition through death.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
summary: A brief free-verse meditation on ownership, vista and the ever-continued journey toward what will yet be supplied; the open road, progress and the self.

title: To --
author: Poe
summary: A short love lyric of dream-visions: the beloved's lips, melody and heart haunt the speaker's sleep, set against the worthlessness of gold. Themes of love, dreams and longing.

title: To --
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A brief love lyric in which the speaker, indifferent to his own desolate lot, is moved that the beloved should sorrow for a mere passer-by. Themes of love, melancholy and transience.

title: To F--
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A love lyric: amid the woes of his earthly path the speaker finds solace in the memory of the beloved, likened to a serene enchanted isle in a stormy sea. Themes of love, consolation and melancholy.

title: To Foreign Lands
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom

title: To Frances S. Osgood
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A short complimentary love lyric counselling the beloved to remain exactly as she is to be endlessly praised and loved. Themes of love, beauty and constancy.

title: To Get the Final Lilt of Songs
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: To fully grasp the great poets one needs old age and the experience it brings as the final faculty.

title: To Helen
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A longer blank-verse love lyric recalling a single moonlit vision of Helen in an enchanted rose-garden, whose haunting eyes guide and enslave the speaker ever after. Themes of idealized love, beauty, eyes and memory.

title: To Helen
author: Poe
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Poe's classic lyric praising Helen's beauty as a Nicean bark bearing the wanderer home to 'the glory that was Greece, and the grandeur that was Rome'. Themes of beauty, idealized love and classical antiquity.

title: To Him That Was Crucified
author: Whitman
summary: Address to Christ as a fellow comrade and equal labourer transmitting the same charge across all lands and creeds; the Christ figure, comradeship, and universal brotherhood.

title: To Isadore
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A musical love lyric celebrating Isadore as a dream-enchantress whose voice and violet eyes wake old memories and turn the speaker's name to melody. Themes of idealized love, beauty, dreams and memory.

title: To Marie Louise (shew)
author: Poe
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: A grateful blank-verse tribute to Marie Louise Shew, whose presence restores the despairing speaker's faith in Truth, Virtue and Humanity, her words echoing the divine 'Let there be light'. Themes of love, gratitude, faith and the angelic beloved.

title: To One Shortly to Die
author: Whitman
summary: Tender address to a dying person, telling them merciless truth yet congratulating their spiritual escape; the corpse is mere excrement, the soul eternal.

title: To One in Paradise
author: Poe
summary: An elegiac love lyric mourning a dead beloved who was the speaker's whole hope; the light of life is now over, his days mere trances. Themes of grief, lost love, mortality and despair.

title: To Rich Givers
author: Whitman
cluster: Wine and Drink · Ballad Ballade · Road
summary: The poet cheerfully accepts modest gifts as he rendezvous with his poems, giving in return the entrance to all the gifts of the universe; free-verse on the open road, the poet and gift.

title: To The States (To Identify the 16th, 17th, or 18th Presidentiad)
author: Whitman
summary: A political lyric of disgust at corrupt antebellum government, prophesying that the sleeping States will awake; a satire of political decay and a call to democratic vigilance.

title: To Thee Old Cause
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Dedication to the deathless cause of liberty for which all wars are fought; the wheel-on-axis image; war, democracy, eternal struggle. Free verse.

title: To Think of Time
author: Whitman
summary: Extended meditation on mortality, burial and time that concludes in defiant affirmation of the eternal soul and universal immortality.

title: To Those Who’ve Fail’d
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse tribute raising a laurel monument to those cut off by early death before their aspirations were realized; themes of failure, death and heroism.

title: To You (Stranger, if you passing meet me)
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand

title: To You
author: Whitman
summary: A direct free-verse address to the unknown reader, affirming the divine worth, identity and unrealized soul of every person; democratic intimacy and the self.

title: To Zante
author: Poe
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A sonnet on the Greek isle of Zante, whose flowery shores now wake only memories of a vanished maiden and entombed hopes; the place is cursed by the refrain 'no more'. Themes of grief, lost love, transience and the classical Mediterranean.

title: To a Certain Cantatrice
author: Whitman
summary: Gift reserved for a hero or rebel is bestowed instead on a singer; music and song, the cause of freedom, the rebel/common artist.

title: To a Certain Civilian
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: A defiant address rejecting the civilian's wish for soft rhymes, affirming the poet's martial, war-born art and his role as singer of the funeral dirge.

title: To a Common Prostitute
author: Whitman
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: Compassionate, scandalous address welcoming the prostitute as Nature welcomes all; the outcast, social injustice, the body, and radical acceptance.

title: To a Foil’d European Revolutionaire
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Consolation to a defeated revolutionary that Liberty waits latent and is the last to leave; revolution, martyrs, defeat made great, and undying liberty.

title: To a Historian
author: Whitman
summary: Opposes the historian of surfaces with himself as chanter of personality projecting the history of the future; prophet-poet, identity, the common man.

title: To a Locomotive in Winter
author: Whitman
summary: Ode addressing a locomotive in a snowstorm as fierce-throated beauty and emblem of modern motion and power, taking the machine as worthy of the Muse.

title: To a President
author: Whitman
summary: A terse rebuke to a president who has not learned the amplitude and impartiality of Nature; free-verse political epigram on the natural order, nation and reform.

title: To a Pupil
author: Whitman
summary: Exhortation that reform requires a magnetic Personality of clean body and soul; reform, the body, identity, and self-culture.

title: To a Stranger
author: Whitman
summary: Address to a passing stranger felt as a long-lost intimate; fleeting urban encounter, recognition, desire, the body and the dream of past shared life.

title: To a Western Boy
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Address to a disciple ('eleve') warning that learning is useless without the blood and silent selection of lovers; comradeship, the body and discipleship.

title: To the East and to the West
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Address across the regions of the States proclaiming a 'superb friendship' latent in all men; comradeship as the purpose of the nation, democracy.

title: To the Garden the World
author: Whitman
summary: Opening of Children of Adam: speaker as new Adam re-ascending to the garden with Eve, celebrating the body and resurrection through love; Edenic, sexual, cyclic.

title: To the Leaven’d Soil They Trod
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Closing Drum-Taps benediction to the American land that witnessed war and peace, the soil and continent nourishing and ripening the poet's songs.

title: To the Man-of-War-Bird
author: Whitman
summary: An apostrophe to the storm-riding frigate-bird as emblem of soul and freedom over sea and sky; free-verse lyric on birds, the sea, storm and the soul.

title: To the Pending Year
author: Whitman
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: A fierce, self-interrogating address to the coming year, the poet searching for a last weapon-word against affectation and his own rebellious self.

title: To the River--
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Beauty · Eyes and Sight
summary: A short love lyric making the clear river an emblem of the beloved's beauty and unhidden heart, her image deep in the speaker's trembling heart. Themes of love, beauty, water and reflection.

title: To the States
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Aphoristic political lyric: resist much, obey little; warns against enslavement and loss of liberty. Democracy, the rebel, reform.

title: To the Sun-Set Breeze
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: The sick, aged poet addresses the cooling evening wind through his window as a spiritual, God-sent messenger linking him to nature and the cosmos.

title: To-Day and Thee
author: Whitman
summary: The whole heirdom of human history and art converges in the present 'thee', a meditation on time and inheritance.

title: Transpositions
author: Whitman
summary: Epigrammatic world-upside-down poem reversing judges and criminals, keepers and prisoners; satirical reformist inversion of social order.

title: Trickle Drops
author: Whitman
summary: Intense Calamus lyric in which 'confession drops' of blood stain every page; blood, confession, shame and the body as the bleeding source of song.

title: True Conquerors
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: Old workers, sailors and soldiers who merely survived their struggles are the true conquerors over all the rest.

title: Turn O Libertad
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Post-war summons to Liberty to turn from the feudal past of kings and slavery toward a democratic future; patriotism, progress, and the rejection of the old order.

title: Twenty Years
author: Whitman
summary: A sailor returns after twenty years circling the globe to find the place changed and parents dead; a meditation on time and homecoming.

title: Ulalume
author: Poe
summary: An incantatory, hauntingly musical ballad: the speaker, wandering a ghoul-haunted October woodland with his Soul (Psyche), is led to the tomb of his lost beloved Ulalume, exactly a year after burying her. Themes of grief, death, memory and the supernatural night-journey.

title: Unfolded out of the Folds
author: Whitman
summary: Litany that man and all his greatness is unfolded out of woman; the great mother, the body, and the generative origin of poems and justice.

title: Unnamed Land
author: Whitman
summary: On the countless vanished nations and unrecorded dead who nonetheless still exist; ubi sunt, mortality, immortality of the soul, and memory.

title: Unseen Buds
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Hidden under snow and ice, infinite germinal buds wait latent throughout earth and cosmos, urging slowly forward in endless unborn becoming.

title: VARIOUS POEMS
author: Shakespeare
summary: A miscellany of short poems attributed to Shakespeare (songs, Passionate Pilgrim pieces, the metaphysical elegy 'The Phoenix and Turtle', and epitaphs) ranging over love, beauty's transience, constancy and mortality.

title: VENUS AND ADONIS
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Greek Mythology · Lust Sexual Desire · Desire
summary: Ovidian erotic narrative poem in sixains: the goddess Venus's failed seduction of the chaste youth Adonis, who is killed by a boar. Central themes: desire and lust, the unattainable beloved, beauty, mortality and transience.

title: Vera, or The Nihilists
author: Wilde
cluster: Swords and Weapons · Power and Corruption · Tyrant
summary: Wilde's first play, a melodramatic political tragedy set in Tsarist Russia about nihilist revolutionaries plotting to assassinate the Czar; Vera's sworn oath to renounce love and pity collides with her love for the Czarevitch, ending in self-sacrifice. Central themes: tyranny and revolution, love versus duty, oath and betrayal, martyrdom.

title: Vigil Strange I Kept on the Field One Night
author: Whitman
summary: A soldier keeps an all-night vigil over the body of a fallen comrade-son and buries him at dawn; an elegy of comradeship, death and love.

title: Virginia--The West
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
summary: An allegory in which the rebellious South lifts a knife against the Mother of All while the loyal West (drest in blue) rushes to her rescue; the Union defended.

title: Vocalism
author: Whitman
summary: On the hard-won divine power to speak words and the magnetic right voice that all things obey; the body, the artist, identity, and song.

title: Von Kempelen and his Discovery
author: Poe
summary: A pseudo-scientific hoax-tale presenting Von Kempelen's alchemical discovery of turning lead into gold and its economic consequences. Themes of gold, science, satire and appearance vs reality.

title: Wandering at Morn
author: Whitman
summary: Morning meditation in which a singing thrush, transmuting grubs and worms into song, becomes a hopeful emblem for the troubled Union's future.

title: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · American Civil War · Battlefield

title: Warble for Lilac-Time
author: Whitman
summary: Joyous spring catalog of returning lilac-time and birds rousing the restless soul to fly forth; spring, flowers, birds, nature, and the soul's longing.

title: Washington’s Monument February, 1885
author: Whitman
summary: Washington's true monument is not marble but the worldwide spirit of freedom, courage and patriotism.

title: We Two Boys Together Clinging
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Exuberant catalogue of two inseparable comrades roaming, mocking statutes and owning no law but themselves; comradeship, the open road, rebellion and the body.

title: We Two, How Long We Were Fool’d
author: Whitman
summary: Two lovers transmuted into all of nature, returning home to freedom and joy; love, nature, eternal return, cosmic identity.

title: Weave in, My Hardy Life
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric using the weaving metaphor to urge ceaseless labor of life in campaigns of peace and war; themes of the soldier, work and life-as-struggle.

title: What Am I After All
author: Whitman
summary: Tiny lyric on the self as a child pleased with the sound of its own name; identity, the self, childhood, and language.

title: What Best I See in Thee
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A free-verse tribute to U. S. Grant whose real greatness lies in carrying the common Western people with him among kings; themes of the common man and democracy.

title: What Place Is Besieged?
author: Whitman
summary: Brief martial allegory: to a besieged place the poet sends an immortal commander with artillery; war imagery, the poet-hero, weapons.

title: What Ship Puzzled at Sea
author: Whitman
summary: Quatrain offering the soul, as a perfect pilot rowing out in a little boat, to guide the puzzled ship of the self into the true channel.

title: What Think You I Take My Pen in Hand?
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Poet records not the battle-ship or great city but two men kissing in parting on a pier; comradely love privileged over public grandeur.

title: When I Heard at the Close of the Day
author: Whitman
cluster: Unrequited Frustrated Love · Unattainable Beloved · Petrarchan Sonnet
summary: Calamus poem contrasting empty public fame with the happiness of lying beside the sleeping beloved by the sea; love, the body, the sea, dawn and autumn imagery.

title: When I Heard the Learn’d Astronomer
author: Whitman
summary: Wearied by the lecturer's charts, the poet wanders out to look in silence at the stars; a free-verse lyric contrasting dry science with mystical wonder, on stars, night and nature.

title: When I Peruse the Conquer’d Fame
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Poet envies not generals or presidents but the 'brotherhood of lovers'; comradeship and faithful love exalted over heroism and worldly fame.

title: When I Read the Book
author: Whitman
summary: Skeptical lyric on the impossibility of biography truly knowing a life, including one's own; identity, memory, the book and writing.

title: When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: Whitman's great pastoral elegy for the assassinated Lincoln, built on the trinity of lilac, fallen western star, and hermit thrush, culminating in a hymn of reconciliation to 'lovely and soothing death.'

title: When the Full-Grown Poet Came
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: An ars-poetica parable of the poet as reconciler standing between Nature and the Soul of man, joining their hands and blending them into one.

title: While Not the Past Forgetting
author: Whitman
summary: Reconciliation poem laying wreaths on the graves of all dead soldiers, North and South, for peace and brotherhood.

title: Whispers of Heavenly Death
author: Whitman
summary: Hushed nocturnal lyric in which murmurs, unseen rivers and a dimmed star intimate a soul passing over as a solemn immortal birth.

title: Who Learns My Lesson Complete?
author: Whitman
summary: Free-verse catalogue addressing all classes of people; meditates on the wonder of the cosmos and the speaker's own immortality, finding ordinary existence equally marvelous.

title: Whoever You Are Holding Me Now in Hand
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · Union · Hands Hand in Hand
summary: Calamus opening poem warning the reader-lover about the cost of comradely love; free-verse meditation on intimacy, elusive identity, and the demanding 'novitiate' of love between comrades.

title: Why the Little Frenchman Wears his Hand in a Sling
author: Poe
summary: A broad dialect comedy narrated in thick Irish brogue by a vain 'Barronitt' courting a widow, who is duped in a hand-holding ruse with a French rival. Themes of farcical satire, vanity and deception.

title: William Wilson
author: Poe
summary: A doppelganger tale: the dissolute narrator is shadowed all his life by a double bearing his own name who thwarts his every vice, until he kills him and destroys himself; the double is his conscience. Themes of the double, conscience, guilt and identity.

title: With All Thy Gifts
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: Apostrophe to a powerful, wealthy America asking whether it lacks the one gift of perfect women and mothers fit for it.

title: With Antecedents
author: Whitman
summary: The present America as the heir and centre of all past ages and civilizations; free-verse on history, time, the common man and self as the meeting point of past and future.

title: With Husky-Haughty Lips, O Sea!
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · Book of Nature · Natural Order
summary: Apostrophe to the sea as a chained, striving kindred soul telling the cosmic tale of elemental passion.

title: World Take Good Notice
author: Whitman
cluster: Poet as Prophet · Prophet · Romantic Movement (Sensibility)
summary: A compressed emblem-lyric of the national flag (thirty-eight stars, scarlet stripes) flaunting a warning to the world; patriotic emblem of the Union and the flag.

title: X-Ing a Paragrab
author: Poe
summary: A comic literary squib: a feud between rival newspaper editors over the letter 'o' ends with a typesetter X-ing out a vowel-laden paragraph into nonsense. Themes of satire of letters, language and folly.

title: Year That Trembled and Reel’d Beneath Me
author: Whitman
cluster: Grief and Loss · Elegy · Clothing and Costume
summary: A brief lyric of the poet shaken by a year of defeat, asking whether he must now chant cold dirges and hymns of defeat; war, grief and the poet's vocation.

title: Year of Meteors (1859-60
author: Whitman
summary: A retrospective chant of a portentous year — John Brown's execution, ships, comets and meteors — the poet himself a transient meteor; free-verse on history, mortality and the nation.

title: Years of the Modern
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · Democracy · Liberty Political Freedom
summary: A visionary free-verse prophecy of a coming democratic world-era, solidarity of races and falling thrones, staged as theatrum mundi; themes of democracy and the new era.

title: Yet, Yet, Ye Downcast Hours
author: Whitman
summary: Poem of dark downcast hours and the dread that matter is conqueror; the dying voices cry out for their destination as the speaker prepares to sail.

title: Yonnondio
author: Whitman
cluster: Ruins the Abbey · Sic Transit Gloria Mundi · Ubi Sunt
summary: A dirge for vanished Native American races who pass like ghosts and disappear unrecorded, a lament of transience.

title: You Felons on Trial in Courts
author: Whitman
summary: Confessional identification of the poet with felons, convicts, and prostitutes, refusing to deny the lusts and wickedness in himself; the outcast, guilt, the body, and social compassion.

title: You Lingering Sparse Leaves of Me
author: Whitman
summary: The poet likens himself to a well-shorn tree's last sparse leaves on winter-nearing boughs, the hardiest and last.

title: Youth, Day, Old Age and Night
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse epigram pairing youth/age and day/night, affirming that old age and the restoring night follow with equal grace.
